Street Racer question bank

questions.stem: Which of the following refers to the transmitting and receiving of data, from voice to video across a distance via a communication channel?
questions.explain: Key: D. Telecommunications is the sending and receiving of data of any kind (voice, text, video) over a distance through a communication channel. A network (C) is tempting, but a network is the set of linked devices that uses telecommunications; it is not the act of transmitting itself. A protocol is a set of rules and a modem is a single device.

questions.stem: Which of the following sequences lists the data storage devices in order of the increasing size of the device?
options: Floppy disk, CDROM, USB flash drive, hard disk
CDROM, USB flash drive, floppy disk, hard disk
USB flash drive, CDROM, hard disk, floppy disk
Hard disk, floppy disk, USB flash drive, CDROM
questions.explain: Key: A. "Size" here means storage capacity: a floppy disk holds about 1.44 MB, a CD-ROM about 700 MB, a USB flash drive several gigabytes and a hard disk hundreds of gigabytes to terabytes. Option B is the most tempting because the CD-ROM is physically larger, but it puts the floppy disk (the smallest capacity) third, so the order is wrong.

questions.stem: One characteristic that books traditionally have as an information source is that they usually
options: provide information on the most current topics
provide an in-depth examination of the topic
take a short time to publish
questions.explain: Key: C. Books are known for depth: they treat a topic in detail and at length. Option B is the trap; books take a long time to write and publish, so they are usually less current than newspapers, journals or websites. Options A and D are also the opposite of what books are like.

questions.stem:
Items 4–5 refer to the following options.

(A) data
(B) wisdom
(C) information
(D) knowledge

Match EACH item below with ONE of the options above. Each option may be used once, more than once or not at all.

The temperatures at three different locations across the country were recorded. The temperatures recorded are an example of
questions.explain: Key: A. Raw, unprocessed readings such as individual temperatures are data. They become information (C) only when processed, for example averaged or compared, so that they carry meaning. That processing has not happened yet in this item.

questions.stem:
Items 4–5 refer to the following options.

(A) data
(B) wisdom
(C) information
(D) knowledge

Match EACH item below with ONE of the options above. Each option may be used once, more than once or not at all.

Susan decided to take along an umbrella with her after learning of the daily average temperature. This is an example of
questions.explain: Key: D. Knowledge is the use of information to make a decision. Susan applied what she learnt to decide to take an umbrella. Information (C) is the tempting choice, because the daily average temperature is information, but the item asks about her decision, which is knowledge.

questions.stem: All of the following are real time communication tools used in information technology EXCEPT
questions.explain: Key: A. A mailing list sends messages to subscribers’ inboxes to be read later, so it is asynchronous, not real time. Internet Relay Chat (B) may look old-fashioned, but it is live text chat, so it is a real-time tool, as are video conferencing and VoIP.

questions.stem: The IEEE/ACM sub-disciplines for computing include all the following EXCEPT
questions.explain: Key: B. The computing sub-disciplines are computer science, computer engineering, software engineering, information systems and information technology. "Artificial technology" is not a discipline; it is a distractor built to sound like artificial intelligence. Information systems (A) is a genuine sub-discipline, even though it sounds more like business.

questions.stem: Miss Jane prepared a practice exam for her class on her personal computer and would like to make this file available on the Internet for her students to download. Which of the following tools should she use to make this file available online?
questions.explain: Key: A. FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is used to upload files to a server so that others can download them. Telnet (B) is tempting because it also connects to a remote computer, but it gives a text-based remote login session; it is not a file upload and download tool.

questions.stem: A large tanker, carrying toxic waste, overturns on a major highway. The Office of Disaster Management needs to inform drivers and the surrounding communities of the disaster. Which of the following information sources is the MOST appropriate to use for sending out the information?
questions.explain: Key: D. Social media spreads an urgent message almost instantly, reaches people on their phones (including drivers already on the road) and is easily shared onward. Television (B) is the strongest distractor, but people must already be watching, and drivers cannot watch television. A newspaper is far too slow, and a website relies on people deciding to visit it.

questions.stem:
Item 10 refers to the following diagram.

What does X represent?
questions.explain: Key: D. The printed CXC key is C (receiver), but X is the device that takes the encoded data from the network PC and sends it out as a signal, so X is the transmitter (D). Y is the channel, where noise enters, and Z, which hands the data on to the remote server, is the receiver. Remember the order sender → transmitter → channel → receiver → destination.

questions.stem: As one of his references, a student used a text book that was written in 1982. Which of the following characteristics of information sources can be challenged by his tutor?
questions.explain: Key: D. Currency is how up to date a source is, and a textbook from 1982 is badly out of date for most IT topics. Reliability (B) is tempting, but a published textbook from a reputable author may still be reliable; the problem the date points to is its age.

questions.stem: What is the name of the first electronic computer?
questions.explain: Key: B. ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer, 1946) is generally named as the first general-purpose electronic computer. The abacus (A) is an early calculating aid, but it is mechanical (beads), not electronic. ARPANET was the forerunner of the Internet, not a computer.

questions.stem:
Which of the following sequences represents the CORRECT timeline of invention for the following hardware technologies?
I. Transistors
II. Vacuum tubes
III. Integrated circuits
questions.explain: Key: D. The computer generations run: first generation, vacuum tubes (1940s); second, transistors (late 1950s); third, integrated circuits (1960s). Option C starts correctly with vacuum tubes but swaps the next two; integrated circuits are made of many transistors, so transistors had to come first.

questions.stem: What is software engineering?
options: A discipline which is concerned with all aspects of software programming.
A discipline which is concerned with all aspects of software production.
A discipline which is concerned with all aspects of software integration.
A discipline which is concerned with all aspects of software modification.
questions.explain: Key: B. Software engineering covers every stage of producing software, from specification and design through coding and testing to maintenance. Programming (A) is the tempting choice, but programming is only one part of production; software engineering is wider than writing code.

questions.stem: The decimal equivalent of the ASCII representation for ‘E’ is 69. What is the ASCII decimal representation for ‘A’?
questions.explain: Key: C. Capital letters have consecutive ASCII codes, so A is four places before E: 69 − 4 = 65. Option B (74) comes from counting forwards instead of backwards (69 + 5), and option A (1) is the letter’s position in the alphabet, not its ASCII code.

questions.stem:
Item 16 refers to the text below.

http://www.cxc.org

The text is an example of
questions.explain: Key: B. A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is the full address of a resource on the web. HTTP (D) is tempting because "http" appears at the start, but that is only the protocol part of the URL; the whole text, protocol plus domain name, is the URL.

questions.stem: Which of the following components are NOT a part of an information system?
questions.explain: Key: B. The components of an information system are hardware, software, data, procedures, users (people) and the network. Reports are an output the system produces, not one of its components. Procedures (D) can look less technical, but they are a component: the rules people follow to use the system.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of HCI is typically used by customers to order food through a drive-through lane at a fast food restaurant?
questions.explain: Key: A. At a drive-through the customer chooses from a fixed list of options on the menu board, which is how a menu-driven interface works. A graphical user interface (C) is tempting if you picture pictures on the board, but a GUI uses windows, icons and a pointer, which the customer does not use.

questions.stem: To convert a document from text into a coded text, ensuring data security, it is BEST to use
questions.explain: Key: A. Encryption scrambles readable text (plaintext) into coded text (ciphertext) that only someone with the key can decode. Biometrics (B) is also a security measure, but it controls who gets in by checking a fingerprint or face; it does not change the document into code.

questions.stem: The physical layout of a network is called a(n)
questions.explain: Key: B. Topology is the arrangement of the devices and connections in a network, for example bus, ring or star. "Design" (A) is too general; a network design includes the topology but also addressing, security and hardware choices.

questions.stem: Reports are produced monthly to show the total number of students registered per course as well as total fees paid. Year-to-date totals are also provided. The type of system that would MOST likely provide this information is a/an
questions.explain: Key: D. A management information system produces regular, scheduled summary reports (monthly totals, year-to-date figures) for middle managers. A transaction processing system (C) is the tempting choice because it records each registration and payment, but it handles the day-to-day transactions; summarising them into routine reports is the job of the MIS.

questions.stem:
Item 22 refers to the following scenario.

SME College used protocols to create a network service on which it provides a set of services for its students. However, a neighbouring school has made a special request to be able to log on remotely so they can have access to some of the services.

Which of the following terms is used to describe connectivity that has been extended to another entity?
questions.explain: Key: C. An extranet is a private network (often an intranet) that gives controlled access to selected outside parties, here the neighbouring school. Intranet (B) is the trap: the college’s own private network for its students is the intranet, but once it is opened to another organisation it becomes an extranet.

questions.stem: Which of the following protocols forms part of a URL?
questions.explain: Key: B. A URL begins with its protocol, as in http://www.cxc.org. TCP/IP (A) is tempting because it carries all Internet traffic, but it works underneath and never appears in the address. SMTP is for sending e-mail.

questions.stem:
Item 24 refers to the following scenario.

A financial company has branches in five different locations throughout the country. At present, each location has a small, internal network for the purpose of sharing resources. Management wants each location to benefit efficiently from the resources available at all other locations.

What is the name given to the network at each branch?
questions.explain: Key: D. The printed CXC key is A (MAN), but a small internal network inside one building or branch is a LAN (D). A MAN covers a city or town, and linking all five branches across the country would create a WAN (C). The scenario asks about the network at each branch, not the network management wants to build, so D is the correct answer.

questions.stem: What type of user interface is commonly utilized by mobile phones?
questions.explain: Key: A. Smartphones use a graphical user interface: icons, windows and touch, which is a form of pointing. Natural language (D) is tempting because phones have voice assistants, but these are an extra feature; the main interface people use is graphical.

questions.stem:
When Janis, a new computer user, installed a program and attempted to use it, she was confused because all she saw on the screen was a green bar with 5 evenly spaced words. When she clicked on each of them, a list of additional words was displayed.

Which HCI is Janis MOST likely using?
questions.explain: Key: B. A bar of words, each opening a list of further choices, is a menu bar with drop-down menus, so the interface is menu-driven. Graphical user interface (A) is tempting because she clicks with a mouse, but there are no icons or windows described, only lists of words to choose from. "Event-driven" describes a programming approach, not a type of HCI.

questions.stem: To access information on the Internet, it would be MOST appropriate to use
questions.explain: Key: D. A web browser retrieves and displays web pages, which is how most information on the Internet is accessed. FTP (A) can fetch files from the Internet, but it is for transferring files, not for viewing and moving between web pages of information.

questions.stem: Ron opened an email and downloaded a document. When he opened the document, the contents were illegible. The document was
questions.explain: Key: B. A document that downloads but shows unreadable, garbled contents has most likely been damaged in transfer, that is, corrupted. Encrypted (A) is the strongest distractor, because an encrypted file also looks like nonsense; however, Ron was not expecting a secured file, and an encrypted file would normally ask for a password or key rather than simply open as gibberish. A protected document would refuse to open or edit, and authenticated describes a confirmed identity, not a file’s contents.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an example of wireless telecommunication transmission media?
questions.explain: Key: D. Fibre optic cable is wired (bounded) media: light travels along a physical glass or plastic cable. Satellite (B) may seem like a "system" rather than a medium, but satellite links send signals through the air as microwaves, so they are wireless, as are radio and microwave.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about web pages are TRUE?
I. They are written using HTTP.
II. Hyperlinks connect web pages to form a website.
III. They can contain multimedia content.
questions.explain: Key: C. Statements II and III are true. Statement I is false: web pages are written in HTML; HTTP is the protocol used to transfer them from the server to the browser. That is why D (all three) is wrong, even though it is tempting.

questions.explain: Key: D. Input and output are shown with a parallelogram, so "read name" goes in a parallelogram. The rectangle (C) is the most tempting, but a rectangle is for a process such as a calculation; the diamond (A) is for a decision and the oval (B) is for start or stop.

questions.stem: The top-level data flow diagram is called the
questions.explain: Key: B. The top-level (level 0) DFD is the context diagram: the whole system as one process, with the external entities and data flows around it. "Data process diagram" (D) sounds plausible because the context diagram shows one process, but it is not a recognised name. The more detailed diagram below it is the level 1 DFD.

questions.stem: The review stage in problem-solving
options: focuses on collecting data from users
involves finding the cost of implementing the system
examines the system to see if any changes are required
questions.explain: Key: D. Review comes after implementation: the solution is evaluated to see whether it works as intended and whether changes are needed. Option B (collecting data from users) is tempting because reviewing may involve user feedback, but collecting data is the focus of the analysis stage, not the purpose of the review.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE about algorithms?
I. Clearly defined and unambiguous
II. Infinite number of steps
III. Problem-solving strategy
questions.explain: Key: B. An algorithm is a problem-solving strategy (a plan for a solution) whose steps are clearly defined and unambiguous. Statement II is false: an algorithm must finish in a finite number of steps. So any option containing II, including D, is wrong.

questions.stem:
Item 35 refers to the table below.

Task No.Task NameMonTueWedThurFriMonTueWedThurFriMon
1Discuss project 
2Assign tasks 
3Gather data    
4Sort relevant data   
5Compile information   

Shaded cells show the days on which each task is scheduled (two working weeks plus the following Monday).

Above is a copy of a Gantt chart used by a group of students to guide them in completing a project. How many TOTAL days will it take to complete tasks 2, 3 and 4?
questions.explain: Key: B. The printed CXC key is A (4), but the chart as shown gives 5. Reading the chart, task 2 runs on Tuesday of week 1, task 3 from Tuesday to Friday of week 1, and task 4 from Thursday of week 1 to Monday of week 2. Tasks 2 to 4 therefore take Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Monday: 5 working days from start to finish (B). Four days is only the length of task 3 on its own. When reading a Gantt chart, count from the first shaded cell of the earliest task to the last shaded cell of the latest task, because tasks can overlap.

questions.stem:
Item 36 refers to the following diagram.

Which of the following flowchart diagrams can be used to represent an IF-THEN-ELSE control structure?
questions.explain: CXC Key: C. Note: the printed key looks doubtful. Only diagram II is a true IF-THEN-ELSE: one decision, a separate action on each branch, and the branches rejoin. Diagram III uses a decision box, but its branch loops back above the decision, so it shows repetition (a loop), and diagram I is plain sequence. None of the options says "II only"; C is the CXC answer because both II and III contain a decision (selection) symbol. Learn the shapes: two branches that rejoin = selection; a line going back up = loop.

questions.explain: Key: B. In a DFD, data must pass through a process before it reaches a data store: Student (external entity) → Accept student info (process) → Student file (data store). Option C is tempting because it has something in the middle, but "data entry clerk" is a person (an entity), not a process, and an entity must not write straight to a data store. Option A also links an entity directly to a store.

questions.stem:
Item 38 refers to the following statement.

FOR J FROM 20 to 15 DO
    WRITE J
END FOR What values would be printed for J?
questions.explain: Key: A. The loop starts at 20 and counts down to 15, and both end values are included, so it writes 20, 19, 18, 17, 16, 15. Option C misses the final value 15; the loop runs while J has not gone past 15, so 15 is still printed. (Strictly, many programming languages need "STEP −1" to count down; without it the loop would not run at all. CXC expects you to read the loop as counting down.)

questions.stem: Into which of the following paradigms are the programming languages C++ classified?
questions.explain: Key: D. C++ was designed as "C with classes" and is classified as an object-oriented language. Procedural (C) is tempting because C++ grew out of C, a procedural language, and can still be written procedurally, but its defining paradigm is object-oriented.

questions.stem:
Item 40 refers to the flowchart below.

Which of the following is the correct pseudocode for the algorithm?
options:
READ Num1,Num2
If Num1 < Num2 Then
Print Num2, Num1
Else
    Num1=Num2
Num2=Num1
Print Num1,Num2
Endif

READ Num1,Num2
If Num1 > Num2 Then
    Print Num2,Num1
    Num1=Num2
    Num2=Num1
    Print Num2, Num1
Endif
questions.explain: Key: D. On the Y (true) branch the flowchart does Num1 = Num2, then Num2 = Num1, then prints Num1, Num2; on the N (false) branch it only prints Num2, Num1. Option D matches this exactly with IF–ELSE. Option A is tempting because its first lines match, but it has no ELSE, so both print statements run when the condition is true and nothing runs when it is false. Option B uses < instead of >, which wrongly sends the case where the numbers are equal to the swap branch.

questions.stem: To gather information from 700 users about the usefulness of a particular system, which of the following tools would be MOST efficient?
questions.explain: Key: C. Questionnaires can be sent to all 700 users at once and the answers gathered and analysed quickly. Interviews (D) give richer detail but would take far too long with 700 people, and observation shows what users do rather than what they think of the system’s usefulness.

questions.stem: Which line of the following algorithm illustrates the control structure of iteration?
questions.explain: Key: C. The printed CXC key is B, but iteration means repetition, and the only line that repeats is the while loop (C): "while 0 < num < 10 do" keeps running its body as long as the condition is true. The "if ... then" line (B) is selection; it tests the condition once and runs its statement at most once.

questions.stem:
Item 43 refers to the diagram below.

From the flow chart above, what action takes place if X > 100?
questions.explain: Key: A. When X > 100 the decision follows the Y (yes) branch to Print (‘Error’), so an error message is displayed. Option C is the trap: X is printed only on the N (no) branch, when X is 100 or less.

questions.stem:
Items 44–45 refer to the following diagram.

What is the final value of A and B when A = 4, B = 3 is the input?
questions.explain: Key: B. A = 4 is greater than B = 3, so the Y branch runs: A = A + B × 2 = 4 + 6 = 10. B is not changed on this branch, so it stays 3. Option D (B = 11) comes from also running the N branch with the new A (3 + 4 × 2 = 11), but only one branch of a decision is taken.

questions.stem:
Items 44–45 refer to the following diagram.

What control structures are used in the data flow diagrams shown?
I. Loop
II. Sequence
III. Selection
questions.explain: Key: D. The steps run in order (input, decide, calculate, output), which is sequence, and the "Is A > B?" decision chooses between two branches, which is selection. There is no loop (I) because no line goes back to an earlier step, so C is wrong. (The item says "data flow diagrams", but the diagram is a flowchart; CXC’s wording is kept.)

questions.stem: A Coralstone College open day features a computer engineer, a computer scientist, a software engineer, an IT specialist and an IS analyst. A visitor asks what all five have in common. Which answer is a genuine commonality?
questions.explain: Key: B. All five use logical problem-solving. Each other option is the specialism of one discipline (CE, IS and CS respectively).

questions.stem: Harbourview Credit Union in Roseau uses software to approve loans automatically. A member whose home was damaged in a hurricane is rejected, although staff believe she will repay. Which limitation of IT does this show?
options: It cannot exercise human judgement in situations its programs do not cover.
It depends on a reliable power supply.
It processes large volumes of applications quickly.
questions.explain: Key: A. The program applies its rules but cannot weigh the member's special circumstances: a lack of human judgement. Dependence on power is a real limitation, but nothing failed here; option D is an advantage of IT, not a limitation.

questions.stem: A Form 6 student is writing a label for a photo of ENIAC (1945) in a Seagrape Bay Secondary School class display. Which characteristic should she list as MOST closely associated with this first-generation computer?
options: High heat output and frequent component failure
questions.explain: Key: D. ENIAC's thousands of vacuum tubes produced great heat and burned out often. Core memory and COBOL belong to the second generation.

questions.stem: In 1982 the owner of a hardware store in Bridgetown, Barbados wants to keep her accounts on a computer, but she cannot program and has no access to a mainframe. Which development in software history MOST allowed users like her to use computers?
options: Packaged application software such as spreadsheets and word processors
questions.explain: Key: C. Packages such as VisiCalc and WordStar let the store owner work on a PC without writing programs. Batch processing still required specialists and a mainframe.

questions.stem: Sorting a cupboard at the Linden Community Centre, a volunteer finds index cards on which "Blue", "17" and "Regent Street" are each written on a separate card, with nothing linking them. In the sense used in the CAPE IT syllabus, these cards hold
options: knowledge, because a volunteer can use them to decide
information, because each card has been written down
information, because the items can be compared
questions.explain: Key: C. The items are separate, unrelated chunks with no connection or context: discrete data. B and D are tempting, but writing items down or being able to compare them does not process them; nothing has been organised or put in context. D confuses possible use with knowledge, which requires information used to make a decision.

questions.stem: Trinidadian Road Survey Team counts vehicles on the San Fernando hill for 10 minutes in every hour instead of continuously. The data collected is BEST described as
questions.explain: Key: C. Counting is an objective measurement (quantitative), and only selected periods are recorded (sampled). A is tempting because counts are quantitative, but the data is not recorded continuously.

questions.stem: Shania, a student at Sea-Almond Secondary School, types "Caribbean history" into her school library's catalogue and gets a list of titles, authors and shelf numbers. The catalogue she used is BEST described as
options: an organised list that describes items and shows where they can be found
a primary source of information about an event
a collection of web pages edited by many users
questions.explain: Key: A. The catalogue is a finding aid that describes items and their location so Shania can fetch them. B describes a journal; C describes a wiki; B is wrong because a catalogue does not report an event.

questions.stem: Kayla, a Lower Six student, interviews her grandmother in Sandy Ground, Anguilla, about how the family got news during Hurricane Irma in 2017. Which pair gives one advantage and one disadvantage of this PERSON as an information source?
options: Follow-up questions can be asked; memories may be inaccurate
questions.explain: Key: A. Kayla can ask follow-up questions (advantage), but her grandmother's memories of 2017 may have faded or changed (disadvantage). C is wrong because people can be biased and are not always available; C describes a CD-ROM.

questions.stem: For her project on the environment, a Breadfruit Valley Secondary student finds a specialist journal article that studies mangrove loss in one lagoon over twenty years with extensive data. Which characteristics BEST describe it?
questions.explain: Key: D. One lagoon is a narrow coverage; twenty years of extensive data is great depth. Option B describes an encyclopaedia-style overview, the opposite.

questions.stem: A student writing a newspaper-style article on household electricity bills in The Bahamas finds a source on tariffs that is available free online, is easy to search, and was published eight years ago. When selecting it to quote CURRENT tariffs, the student should be MOST concerned about its
questions.explain: Key: A. Tariffs change, so eight-year-old figures fail the currency criterion. Availability and cost are favourable here and are not the concern.

questions.stem: At Sea-Almond Secondary School, the head of Mathematics reviews the term mark sheet and asks teachers to record marks for each question, not just totals, from next term. This is an example of which stage of the information processing cycle?
questions.explain: Key: B. Evaluating the output and changing what is collected at input is feedback. Output is tempting because a mark sheet is involved, but the action described is the evaluation and update that loops back to input.

questions.stem: The owner of the Sunset Travel Agency in Gros Islet is comparing the systems used by businesses she deals with. Which of these is an example of an AUTOMATED information system?
options: A handwritten ledger in a corner shop
An airline reservation system shared by agents and websites
A card catalogue in a school library
A paper register marked each morning by a form teacher
questions.explain: Key: B. A reservation system is computer-based and shared over networks, so the agency can book seats instantly. The card catalogue is a common distractor because libraries can be automated, but a card catalogue itself is manual.

questions.stem: Bayside Resort in Grace Bay plans to replace its paper payroll ledger with a payroll database. The finance manager warns that new computers, software and staff training must all be paid for before any savings are seen. Which disadvantage of automated processing is she describing?
options: It is costly to set up
questions.explain: Key: C. Paying for hardware, software and training before any benefit is the cost of setting up. Option B is tempting because staff will rely on the system, but the manager's warning is about money spent at the start, and option D reverses a benefit: automated data is reusable.

questions.stem: Island Link Ferry Company stores the number of passengers on its smallest water taxi in a 6-bit field. What is the largest passenger count the field can hold?
questions.explain: Key: A. 6 bits give 2⁶ = 64 patterns, numbered 0 to 63, so the largest passenger count is 63 (111111). 64 is the number of patterns, not the largest value.

questions.stem: Harbour View Hotel wants to show its board what share of guests came from each region last year. Which representation is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: A. A pie chart shows parts of a whole, which is exactly what "share of guests" means. A line graph is tempting, but it is used for change over time, not proportions.

questions.stem: The CEO of Caribe Marts group opens a single screen of charts comparing group sales in Antigua, Barbuda and St. Kitts with regional visitor arrivals, then taps one island's figure to see its individual stores. Which type of information system is she using?
questions.explain: Key: C. A senior executive viewing a graphical summary of internal and external data, with drill-down to individual stores, is using an EIS. A is tempting because an MIS also summarises, but it serves middle managers with routine internal reports.

questions.stem: Bayview Supermarket in Holetown offers credit accounts to local restaurants. At month end its system lists ONLY those customers whose accounts are more than 60 days overdue. Which type of report is this?
questions.explain: Key: D. Only records meeting a condition outside normal limits are shown, which defines an exception report. C is tempting because each customer is listed individually, but a detailed report would list every account, not only overdue ones.

questions.stem: The office computer at the Harbour Gems Jewellers has an old hard disk. A technician runs a program that gathers the scattered parts of each file into one continuous area so files load faster. This program is BEST classified as
questions.explain: Key: A. The technician’s program is a disk defragmenter: it performs one maintenance task, so it is a utility. It is often bundled with the operating system, which makes B tempting, but it is not the OS itself.

questions.stem: An engineer at Caribbean Pump Works in Trinidad writes the code for a water-pump controller using mnemonics such as LOAD, ADD and STORE, then runs an assembler on it. The assembler
options: translates a high-level program one statement at a time
loads the operating system when the controller starts
translates the assembly language mnemonics into machine code
copies the code files to a backup device
questions.explain: Key: C. An assembler translates the engineer’s low-level assembly language into machine code. A describes an interpreter, a common confusion because both are translators.

questions.stem: The managing director of Windward Air, based at Piarco Airport, studies a chart of passenger numbers over ten years together with regional tourism forecasts. At which decision-making level is this information MOST likely used?
questions.explain: Key: C. Long-term, summarised, external and future-oriented information supports strategic decisions. A is tempting because charts and summaries also appear at the tactical level, but ten-year trends and external forecasts point to top management.

questions.stem: Frigate Bay Marina replaces its command line booking system with a graphical user interface after newly hired dock staff struggle to use it. Which disadvantage of the command line BEST explains this change?
options: It needs more memory and processing power.
Users must remember commands and their exact syntax.
It cannot be used to automate tasks.
It is slower for expert users.
questions.explain: Key: B. The new dock staff are novices, and recalling exact commands makes a CLI hard for them. A and D are the reverse of the truth: a CLI uses fewer resources and is faster for experts; C is wrong because scripts automate tasks.

questions.stem: Seaside Pharmacy in Gros Islet redesigns its customer registration form so all labels line up on one edge and all input boxes sit in a single column. This design follows the principle of
questions.explain: Key: C. Placing elements on shared lines is alignment. Ease of learning (D) may improve as a result, but the principle being applied is alignment.

questions.stem: Saba Dive Shop's booking website shows full dates in red and available dates in green, with no other indicator. Which customers are MOST disadvantaged when they try to book a dive?
questions.explain: Key: A. They cannot tell the two colours apart, so the meaning is lost. Hearing impairment (B) is not relevant because the information is visual.

questions.stem: An accountant at the Portsmouth Marine Supplies uses her home Internet connection to reach the office server. Her data is encrypted in a "tunnel" before it leaves her laptop. What is she using?
questions.explain: Key: D. An encrypted tunnel over a public network such as the Internet is a VPN. B covers a city, C is a public place offering Wi-Fi (and would be riskier without a VPN) and D is a configuration of equal computers.

questions.stem: Frigate Bay Tours office upgrades its Internet connection from 20 Mbps to 200 Mbps so that all staff can stream training videos at once. Which statement about the characteristic that has improved is correct?
options: It is the direction in which data flows
It is measured in bits per second for digital channels
It is the layout of nodes in a network
It is the process of varying a carrier wave
questions.explain: Key: B. The office has increased its bandwidth, the channel's capacity, which is measured in bits per second. A is topology, B is communication mode and D is modulation.

questions.stem: Ms. Richardson, a teacher at Hummingbird Ridge High School, finishes a report and clicks Send in her email program. Which protocol carries the email from her computer to the school’s mail server?
questions.explain: Key: B. SMTP sends email from Ms. Richardson’s client to the mail server. POP3 and IMAP are tempting but they retrieve email from the server; FTP transfers files.

questions.stem: The administrator at the English Harbour Car Rental office discovers that the router still uses its factory login, "admin". Which security measure should be applied FIRST to stop staff and customers changing the router settings?
questions.explain: Key: B. The router (administrator) password protects the settings page, so changing "admin" closes the gap at the car rental office. WPA3 is tempting, but it protects wireless traffic, not access to the router configuration.

questions.stem: A technician at the Seaside Pharmacy in Gros Islet wants data sent over the staff Wi-Fi to be scrambled, so that a customer capturing the signal in the shop cannot read it. Which setting is the encryption algorithm that does this?
questions.explain: Key: D. AES is the encryption algorithm used by WPA2 and WPA3 to scramble the pharmacy's wireless data. MAC filtering is tempting because it is also a security setting, but it controls which devices may join; it does not encrypt data.

questions.stem: The manager of the Ambergris Caye Ferry Desk notes that the RAM in the office desktop can be upgraded in five minutes, but the RAM in a sealed laptop cannot be changed at all. Which feature of IS components is she MOST directly comparing?
questions.explain: Key: C. Ease of repair and upgrade is maintainability. Storage is tempting because RAM holds data, but the manager is comparing how easily the part can be changed, not its capacity.

questions.stem: When teachers at Bayleaf Hill Secondary in Port of Spain enter end-of-term marks, the grade system rejects any mark below 0 or above 100. This check mainly helps to maintain
questions.explain: Key: D. The 0 to 100 rule is a range check, a form of validation, which keeps data accurate and so protects data integrity. Data security is tempting, but security concerns unauthorised access or loss, not whether entered values are reasonable.

questions.stem: A Grade 12 class at Calabash Point Secondary is reviewing four lines written about local problems around the Caribbean. Which line describes only a SYMPTOM rather than stating the problem?
options: Double bookings leave five groups a week waiting, which will cost the company customers.
Tomato leaves are curling and turning yellow.
Whitefly is cutting the farmer's harvest by a third, and she will lose her contracts if it continues.
Patients are turned away twice a week because stock levels are unknown, so they may miss medication.
questions.explain: Key: B. Curling, yellow leaves are a visible sign only; they do not say who is affected, the cause, or the consequence. B, C and D each contain the parts of a problem statement.

questions.stem: Six months after installing a new fuel-ordering system, the Sea Breeze Marina finds boats still waiting for fuel on busy weekends, so the manager goes back to analyse the causes again. Why is evaluation and review said to make problem-solving a cycle?
options: It repeats the implementation stage exactly.
Its feedback may send the problem-solver back to an earlier stage.
It replaces the need to analyse the problem.
It must be completed before the problem is defined.
questions.explain: Key: B. The marina's review showed the problem was not fully solved, and that feedback sent the manager back to analysis. B reverses the order of the stages: evaluation and review comes last, not before definition.

questions.stem: A Curaçao hotel is deciding whether to build an online booking system. A manager's claim that "guests prefer to book online", with no booking figures behind it, is BEST classified as
questions.explain: Key: B. It looks like useful demand information but masks the missing booking figures, so it cannot guide the decision. Desirable is tempting, but desirable information genuinely helps the decision; this claim only appears to.

questions.stem: A sales report given to the manager of the Island Hardware chain in St. Lucia shows figures for only three of its four branches. The report is MOST weakened by a lack of
questions.explain: Key: B. A branch is missing, so the information is incomplete. Accuracy may come to mind, but the figures that are present may be correct; the problem is the gap.

questions.stem: A Sandbox Tree College student needs evidence on how sea temperature affects coral near Tobago. She has a tourism magazine feature, a dive shop's blog, a local newspaper report and an article in a scholarly marine science journal. Applying the level of scholarship criterion, which should carry the MOST weight?
options: The journal article, because it is written for specialists and gives in-depth analysis
All four equally, because they cover the same topic
The dive shop blog, because the owner dives there every week
The magazine feature, because it is the easiest to understand
questions.explain: Key: A. Scholarly publications are written for specialists and give in-depth analysis, so they should carry the main weight in research that needs evidence. Option D is tempting because general-audience material is easier to read, but it may lack in-depth analysis.

questions.stem: Nevis Ferry Line wants its booking system to go live within six weeks with seat booking only, adding online payment and a loyalty scheme later. Which model BEST suits this?
questions.explain: Key: A. Delivering the core (seat booking) first and adding parts later is incremental development. Throwaway prototyping (C) clarifies requirements but does not deliver a working system.

questions.stem: The Port of Spain Water Taxi booking system was delivered as seat booking, then payments, then loyalty points, and its booking screen was reworked over several cycles. Which statement CORRECTLY distinguishes iterative from incremental development?
options: Iterative and incremental development are identical terms
Iterative development repeats the cycle to refine the product, whereas incremental development delivers the system in parts that add functionality
Iterative development delivers the system once, whereas incremental development never delivers a complete system
Iterative development is used only for hardware, whereas incremental development is used only for software
questions.explain: Key: B. Iterative = repeating and refining; incremental = adding working parts. Option A is a common misconception because the two are often used together.

questions.stem: Portsmouth Water Taxi compares the USD 18,000 cost of an online ticketing system with the USD 9,000 a year it should save in cash handling. This cost-benefit analysis is MOST closely associated with which type of feasibility?
questions.explain: Key: B. Asking whether benefits justify cost is economic feasibility. Operational (C) asks whether the system fits existing procedures, such as the boarding routine, not money.

questions.stem: Sunrise Canteen app at a Roseau secondary school lets students order meal vouchers, entered as a whole number from 1 to 50. Which set contains ONLY boundary test data?
questions.explain: Key: A. 1 and 50 are at the edges of the valid range. D is tempting, but 0 and 51 lie just outside the range, so they are erroneous data the system should reject.

questions.stem: Guadeloupe Ferry Service sets fares using five yes/no conditions: resident? under 12? over 65? return trip? peak season? The analyst records the rule in a limited-entry decision table. How many rules does the complete table contain?
questions.explain: Key: A. Rules = 2 to the power 5 = 32. B (25) is tempting for candidates who square the number of conditions instead of raising 2 to that power.

questions.stem: Before any code is written for a Port of Spain supermarket's checkout system, a developer at the Trinidad Web Works writes "IF total > 500 THEN apply discount ENDIF" and draws a matching diagram of diamonds and boxes. In which stage of the SDLC are these tools MAINLY being used?
questions.explain: Key: A. The developer's pseudocode and flowchart represent the logic of the solution before it is coded, which is design. Implementation (B) is tempting but concerns installing the finished system and changeover.

questions.stem: The context diagram for the Blue Channel Ferries booking system shows six external data flows. The analyst now draws the level 1 DFD and must make sure it is balanced. A level 1 DFD is balanced with its context level DFD when it
options: has exactly the same number of processes
has no processes that read from data stores
has the same external entities and the same input and output data flows
has the same number of data stores as entities
questions.explain: Key: C. All six ferry flows must reappear with the same entities. A is tempting, but the context level has one process and level 1 has several, so the numbers are never the same.

questions.stem: At Frigate Bay Hardware, process 2.0 "Check stock" receives an item code from Customer and reads stock levels from D1 Stock, but the draft DFD shows no outgoing data flow. What error is this?
questions.explain: Key: D. The stock check result disappears: inputs but no outputs is a black hole. A (miracle) is the reverse pattern and is the most common confusion.

questions.stem: A Frangipani Hill Academy marks program must add a student's two coursework marks, mark1 and mark2, and store the result in a variable called total. Which pseudocode statement does this correctly?
questions.explain: Key: A. The assignment arrow stores the value on the right in the variable on the left. Option C is tempting because it mentions both marks, but INPUT reads data; it does not calculate.

questions.stem: The Jamaican courier firm Island Parcels gives its drivers the instruction "If the parcel is heavy, charge extra." Which change would make the step clearly defined and unambiguous?
options: If the parcel weighs more than 5 kg, add $10 to the charge.
If the parcel seems heavy to the driver, charge a fair amount extra.
If the parcel is very heavy, charge a lot extra.
questions.explain: Key: B. An exact weight and an exact amount give one meaning only. Option D is tempting because "very" sounds more precise, but it is still vague.

questions.stem: A cruise passenger's tablet bought in Germany connects instantly to the free network at the Castries cruise pier, even though the pier's access points come from a different manufacturer. Both follow IEEE 802.11. This standard defines
options: the rules of the A.M. Turing Award
questions.explain: Key: C. IEEE 802.11 defines Wi-Fi, which lets the tablet and the pier's access points work together. Wired Ethernet is the most tempting distractor, but that is IEEE 802.3; the Turing Award belongs to ACM and CITP to BCS.

questions.stem: Darnell, a Computer Science student from Dominica, is told by his lecturer to join the Association for Computing Machinery (ACM) as a student member. ACM is BEST described as
options: an organisation for Information Systems academics only
a UK chartered institute that licenses IT professionals by law
a body that sets electrical safety standards for power utilities
an educational and scientific computing society that publishes research and promotes ethics
questions.explain: Key: D. ACM is the largest educational and scientific computing society, with a Digital Library and Code of Ethics that would serve Darnell well. Option A describes AIS more closely, and option B confuses ACM with BCS.

questions.stem: In 1965 a university physics laboratory buys a cabinet-sized DEC PDP-8. It costs far less than a mainframe and is shared only by staff in that one department. The PDP-8 is BEST classified as a
questions.explain: Key: D. A cabinet-sized, relatively cheap machine serving one department is the classic minicomputer. It predates the microprocessor, so it is not a microcomputer.

questions.stem: An engineering student at Flamboyant Heights College reads that the Intel 4004 (1971) held a complete central processing unit on one small piece of silicon. Which development does this describe?
questions.explain: Key: A. A CPU on one chip is a microprocessor. The transistor is a single switch, the building block of chips.

questions.stem: Island Pulse news website in Jamaica starts a graph's vertical axis at 98 so that a 2% rise in supermarket prices looks like a dramatic jump. This is an example of information that is
questions.explain: Key: A. The figures are accurate but Island Pulse presents them misleadingly, hiding their true size, so the information is disguised. Inconsistency (B) would require two sources that contradict each other.

questions.stem: Caribbean Credit Check Ltd collects repayment histories and charges banks in Barbados and St. Kitts a fee for each credit report it supplies. Which of the following BEST explains why this information is a commodity?
options: It can be shared with many banks without being used up.
It can be presented as a table or as a chart.
It is bought, sold and traded for value.
It loses its usefulness as repayment histories change.
questions.explain: Key: C. The company sells the reports for a fee: a commodity is something traded for value. B describes shareability, the most tempting distractor because many banks receive reports; C describes lifespan; D describes format.

questions.stem: Breadfruit Valley Secondary in the Guyana interior has no Internet access. Which of the following is an ADVANTAGE of a DVD of science lessons as an information source for this school?
options: It can deliver video and audio offline.
It needs no player or computer.
questions.explain: Key: C. A DVD stores multimedia and works without the Internet, which suits the school. B is wrong because disc content is fixed; D is tempting, but the school still needs a DVD player or computer.

questions.stem: Mr. Richardson, the owner of a small electronics shop on Bridge Street, wants a readable, illustrated review of the latest laptops before he orders stock. Which source is MOST suitable for him?
options: A research journal on processor design
Raw sales data from a supplier
questions.explain: Key: A. Magazines are written for general readers, with reviews and illustrations. B is tempting because it is expert, but journals are technical and written for specialists, not a shop owner choosing stock.

questions.stem: A Breadfruit Valley Secondary student finds a page claiming to be the official exam timetable. It has no author's name and was changed twice last week. Which characteristic of information on the Internet MOST affects whether she should select it?
options: Content can be published by anyone and changed or removed at any time.
All online content is peer reviewed.
Online content is always more accurate than print.
questions.explain: Key: A. The anonymous, frequently changed page shows the lack of gatekeeping and changeable content that define Internet information, so she should confirm the timetable with the school. The other options are common misconceptions.

questions.stem: Harbourview Planning Group is preparing a public briefing on a hypothetical extension to the cruise pier in Kingston. Which source is MOST likely to show bias on the benefits of the extension?
options: A press release from the company contracted to build the extension
A refereed study of cruise tourism’s economic effects
A statistics table of cruise passenger arrivals by year
A dictionary definition of a cruise pier
questions.explain: Key: A. The building contractor gains from the project going ahead, so it has a clear interest. The refereed study (B) is tempting because it is on the same topic, but independent expert review reduces bias.

questions.stem: Dominica Carnival Committee has finished processing the parade results. Volunteers now post the results on the committee's website, send them by SMS to every troupe leader and pin a printed copy at the Carnival Village. Which activity is being carried out?
options: Capturing data at the point where it occurs
Collating the scores from several judges
Dissemination of information to its users
Storing the results for later retrieval
questions.explain: Key: C. Posting, texting and pinning up the results distributes information to its audience, which is dissemination (part of output). Option B describes collating, which is often confused with dissemination because both involve moving data around, but collating brings data together rather than sending it out.

questions.stem: Bayside Property Agency in Bridgetown keeps 10,000 paper property records filed by owner surname and is considering moving them to a searchable database. Which statement about manual and automated retrieval is CORRECT?
options: Automated retrieval can only be performed by one user at a time.
Automated retrieval requires records to be physically re-sorted first.
Manual retrieval is equally fast for any field in the record.
Manual retrieval is fast only by the filing key, while automated retrieval can search by any field.
questions.explain: Key: D. The agency's paper file has one fixed order, so only the surname key gives fast retrieval; a database can query any field, such as street or price. Option B is a misconception carried over from paper systems: software sorts or filters without moving stored data.

questions.stem: Every month the Island Savings Bank in Georgetown runs the same interest calculation and prints statements for 20,000 account holders. Which statement BEST describes the data the bank is processing?
options: Scientific data: it requires numerous computations on each reading
Scientific data: its output must be generated within seconds
Business data: it is repeatedly processed and needs large volumes of output
Business data: it needs few repetitions but very fast output
questions.explain: Key: C. Statements are produced by the same processing every month, in large volumes, which is the mark of business data. Option A is tempting because interest involves calculation, but scientific data needs numerous complex computations and fast output, as in storm forecasting.

questions.stem: A cashier at the Grand Anse Mini Mart sells 37 bottles of water in one morning, and the till stores this count as an 8-bit binary number. Which pattern is stored?
questions.explain: Key: D. 37 = 32 + 4 + 1, giving 00100101. 10100100 is the correct bits written in reverse, the result of reading division remainders from the top down.

questions.stem: A telecoms company customer service trainee is writing notes on how a phone stores the text of an SMS message. Which statement about ASCII in her notes is correct?
options: The upper-case letters A to Z have consecutive codes from 65 to 90.
The character '9' is stored as the binary number 00001001.
Each character is represented by a sequence of dots and dashes.
Lower-case letters have codes 32 lower than their upper-case versions.
questions.explain: Key: A. A to Z run consecutively from 65 to 90. Lower case is 32 higher, not lower; dots and dashes are Morse; and the character '9' has code 57, not the value 9.

questions.stem: A nurse at a clinic on Saba enters a patient's fever, rash and joint pain into an expert system. The system checks its stored IF ... THEN rules against these symptoms and suggests a blood test for dengue. Which part of the expert system applied the rules to the symptoms?
questions.explain: Key: B. The inference engine applied the rules to the nurse's facts to reach the suggestion. C is tempting, but the knowledge base only stores the rules; it does not apply them.

questions.stem: At the Harbour Hardware store in Nassau, every sale recorded at the tills during the week is later totalled by department in a report for the store manager. Which statement BEST describes the relationship between the TPS and the MIS here?
options: The output of the TPS becomes the input of the MIS.
The TPS and MIS use completely separate data.
The MIS records transactions that the TPS later summarises.
The MIS replaces the TPS once reports are needed.
questions.explain: Key: A. The MIS totals the sales that the store's TPS has already captured and processed at the tills. C is tempting but reverses the roles: the TPS records transactions and the MIS summarises them.

questions.stem: A clerk at the Bridgetown Shipping Agency has email, a spreadsheet and a payroll package open at once on her Windows laptop. Which of these tasks is carried out by the OPERATING SYSTEM?
options: Converting assembly language into machine code
Allocating memory to each of the programs that are running
questions.explain: Key: D. Giving each of the clerk’s open programs its own memory is memory management, a core OS function. C is tempting because it is system software, but converting assembly language is the job of an assembler, a language translator.

questions.stem: Nevis Ferry Link, which carries passengers and cargo between Basseterre and Charlestown, is deciding whether to commission bespoke ticketing software or buy an off-the-shelf package. What is the MAIN advantage of the bespoke option?
options: It is designed to meet the ferry company’s exact requirements
It has been tested by thousands of users
questions.explain: Key: B. Bespoke software would be written for the ferry company’s own mix of passengers, cargo and day trips. A, B and D are all advantages of off-the-shelf software, which is why they tempt candidates who reverse the comparison.

questions.stem: At the San Pedro Hardware store, the stock system automatically reorders plywood whenever fewer than 40 sheets remain, and it makes the same choice every time. Which feature of a structured decision does this show?
options: It is made only once, in response to a new situation.
It depends mainly on the intuition of senior managers.
It follows a well-defined procedure and can often be automated.
It relies on incomplete and uncertain external information.
questions.explain: Key: C. The plywood reorder follows a fixed rule (below 40 sheets), so the stock system can make it automatically. A, C and D describe unstructured decisions; A is tempting because the rule is clear, but structured decisions like this are repetitive, not one-off.

questions.stem: The online registration screen of Breadfruit Valley Secondary contains boxes labelled Name, Date of Birth and Address, and a drop-down list for Form Level. Which type of HCI is this?
questions.explain: Key: A. Labelled fields for data entry define a form-based interface. C is tempting because of the drop-down list, but that is only one control inside a form whose purpose is collecting several items of data.

questions.stem: Flamboyant Heights College is adding menus, step-by-step wizards and tooltips to its student portal for students logging in during their first week. Which group of users will MOST benefit?
questions.explain: Key: C. Guidance features suit users who are new or occasional, like first-week students. Expert users (B) find forced wizards slow and prefer shortcuts.

questions.stem: Frigate Bay Logistics plans a new parcel-tracking system and hires Devon, a systems analyst. Which statement BEST describes what Devon will do?
options: Use keyboard shortcuts to process parcel transactions quickly
Repair printers and reset passwords for warehouse staff
Study the company's problem and specify what the new system must do
Enter customer orders into the sales system
questions.explain: Key: C. Analysing requirements is the analyst's role. Option B is tempting because it is also an IT professional's job, but it describes technical support.

questions.stem: A student in Gros Islet connects her home computer to the Internet over a telephone line. A device converts the computer's digital data into analogue signals for the line and back again. The device is needed because it
options: converts between digital and analogue signals
sends data only to the correct MAC address
increases the bandwidth of the line
questions.explain: Key: A. The student's modem modulates digital data onto an analogue carrier for the telephone line and demodulates incoming signals. A describes a firewall, C a switch; a modem cannot increase the line's bandwidth.

questions.stem: Leeward Wholesale in St. George's lets its approved shop customers on Carriacou and Petite Martinique log in to its private network to check stock and place orders. This arrangement is
questions.explain: Key: A. Giving authorised outsiders, the shop customers, access to part of a private network is an extranet. A (intranet) is tempting but an intranet is restricted to the wholesaler's own staff.

questions.stem: A technician at Caribbean Connect ISP in Kingston captures traffic on the office LAN and sees units of data carrying source and destination MAC addresses and an error-checking trailer. At the Data Link layer of the OSI model, this protocol data unit (PDU) is called a
questions.explain: Key: D. Units with MAC addresses and a trailer are frames, the Data Link PDU. Packet is the most tempting distractor, but packets carry IP addresses and belong to the Network layer.

questions.stem: A lecturer at Flamboyant Heights College asks her class to compare the two networking models in one line of a revision table. Which statement BEST distinguishes the OSI model from the TCP/IP model?
options: The OSI model is used by the Internet, whereas the TCP/IP model is only theoretical.
The OSI model has no Transport layer, whereas the TCP/IP model does.
The OSI model has seven layers, whereas the TCP/IP model has four.
The OSI model combines the Data Link and Physical layers, whereas the TCP/IP model separates them.
questions.explain: Key: C. OSI has seven layers and TCP/IP four, a correct contrast on the same feature for the revision table. Option D is tempting but reversed: TCP/IP combines Data Link and Physical into Network Access.

questions.stem: Kemar is setting up a new router for his family's snack shop on Bridge Street, Castries. The cable from the ISP's modem should be connected to the router's
questions.explain: Key: D. The WAN port connects Kemar's router to the wide area network (the ISP). A LAN port is tempting because it is the same shape, but LAN ports are for the shop's local devices.

questions.stem: At the Frigate Bay Tours office, a speed test on Wi-Fi gives 15 Mbps, while the same laptop cabled to the router gives 92 Mbps on a 100 Mbps plan. What should the technician conclude?
options: The ISP is delivering far less than the plan.
The wireless link is the bottleneck.
questions.explain: Key: C. The office's wired result is close to the plan, so the line is fine and the Wi-Fi link is limiting speed. Blaming the ISP is tempting, but the wired test proves the ISP is delivering.

questions.stem: Bayside Credit Union in English Harbour must choose between swipe cards and fingerprint readers for its vault-room door. Which statement BEST compares the two options?
options: Swipe cards cannot record entries, whereas biometrics always can.
A swipe card is a logical control, whereas a biometric is always a physical control.
A swipe card checks something the user has, whereas a biometric checks something the user is.
A swipe card cannot be cancelled if lost, whereas a biometric can be reset.
questions.explain: Key: C. Cards prove possession; biometrics prove a physical or behavioural characteristic. Option D is tempting but reversed: a lost card is easily cancelled, whereas a stolen biometric template cannot be changed.

questions.stem: Ambergris Caye Ferry Desk must choose between a free paper sign-up sheet that keeps getting lost, a mid-priced online booking tool that meets all its requirements, and the newest system, priced far above its budget. The "optimal solution" is the one that
options: gives the best overall fit to the requirements and constraints
was suggested first by the person who owns the problem
questions.explain: Key: B. Optimal means the best balance of criteria for this problem, which here is the mid-priced tool that meets the requirements within budget. A is a common misconception: the free sign-up sheet is cheapest but keeps getting lost, so it fails to solve the problem.

questions.stem: A Sixth Form student studying Gros Islet Mini Mart, where shelves are often empty because stock is counted by hand, writes: "The problem is that the shop needs a barcode scanner." What is the MAIN weakness of this problem statement?
options: It is written in the present tense.
It names a solution instead of describing the problem.
questions.explain: Key: D. A problem statement must be solution-neutral; naming a scanner closes off other options. B is tempting, but technology may appear in a statement as long as the statement describes the problem rather than the fix.

questions.stem: Four groups bring problems to a community IT fair at Coralstone College. Which group is dealing with a scientific problem?
options: A dive team measuring sea temperatures to explain coral bleaching near Tobago
A community council planning a programme to reduce youth crime
A Grand Anse restaurant choosing prices for a new menu
A student deciding which laptop to buy for school
questions.explain: Key: A. The dive team investigates through measurement and observation. Option B is tempting because it uses data, but it is a social problem owned by the community.

questions.stem: As a hurricane approaches St. Kitts, a forwarded voice note falsely claiming that "all the shelters are already full" reaches thousands of phones within an hour. Which characteristic of information on the Internet MOST explains this?
options: Search engines rank pages by accuracy.
Content can be easily copied and shared by anyone.
Online information always shows its publication date.
questions.explain: Key: B. Easy copying and sharing lets unverified claims spread rapidly. Option A is a common misconception: ranking reflects popularity and other factors, not accuracy.

questions.stem: A CAPE student in St. John’s finds dengue prevention advice at the address www.healthtips-host.com/~rjames/dengue.html. The page has no Webmaster contact and no update date, and no reliable site links to it. Which conclusion is MOST justified?
options: It is refereed, because it has been published on the Internet.
It is an academic page, because the address contains a tilde.
It must be current, because web pages are updated every day.
It is probably a private individual's page without organisational approval, so it should be verified before use.
questions.explain: Key: D. The tilde and personal name point to a private individual, and there is no sign of organisational approval, currency or links from reliable pages. Option B reverses the clue: a tilde usually marks a personal page, not an academic one.

questions.stem: Sales staff at the Broad Street Jewellers try a clickable model of a tablet catalogue with cruise passengers over a weekend and report two missing functions. Which ADVANTAGE of the prototyping model does this show?
options: User involvement is no longer needed
Final costs become easy to predict at the start
Thorough documentation is produced at every stage
Users identify missing functions and usability problems early
questions.explain: Key: D. The staff evaluated a working model early, so problems surfaced early. Option B is tempting, but prototyping is hard to cost because the number of cycles is unknown.

questions.stem: Anguilla Port Authority used Waterfall for its cargo manifest system. During final testing, staff discover that a field required by Customs was missed at the analysis stage. This illustrates which DISADVANTAGE of Waterfall?
options: Errors in the requirements may not be discovered until testing, when they are costly to fix
It delivers working software too often
It cannot be used for large projects
It is difficult to understand and manage
questions.explain: Key: A. Testing comes late, so the missed Customs field surfaced late and is expensive to fix. Option D is wrong: Waterfall is one of the simplest models to understand and manage.

questions.stem: A Trinidad payroll department runs its old and new systems together for three pay periods. The MAIN disadvantage of this approach is that
options: there is no fallback if the new system fails
only one department can use the new system
old and new modules must exchange data during the changeover
staff must carry out every task twice, increasing cost and workload
questions.explain: Key: D. Parallel running doubles the workload. A describes direct changeover; D describes a problem of phased implementation.

questions.stem: Albert Street Code tells a client: "Our programmers write the code, but our process also covers specification, design, testing, documentation and maintenance." Which statement BEST distinguishes software engineering from programming?
options: Software engineering uses only high-level languages.
Software engineering applies only to hardware design.
Software engineering is a systematic, disciplined approach covering specification, design, testing, documentation and maintenance, of which programming is one part.
Programming produces documentation, whereas software engineering produces code.
questions.explain: Key: C. As Albert Street Code explains, programming is one activity within the wider discipline of software engineering. C reverses the relationship: software engineering includes both code and documentation.

questions.stem: At Guyana Rice Exporters in Georgetown, an analyst studies the company's procedures manual and order forms. Staff later explain that half of those procedures were dropped when a new manager arrived. Which limitation of reviewing printed material does this illustrate?
options: Staff change their behaviour when documents are read.
Documents may be out of date and not reflect current practice.
It produces only quantitative data from rating scales.
It requires the analyst to schedule meetings with every user.
questions.explain: Key: B. The Guyana Rice Exporters manual describes procedures no longer followed, so the documents are out of date. B confuses this tool with the Hawthorne effect of observation.

questions.stem: An analyst at the Dominica Credit Union in Roseau must present the loan-approval rules to the board, whose members have no technical training. She decides to use a decision tree instead of a decision table. Which advantage of the tree supports her decision?
options: It makes it easier to check that all 2 to the power n rules are present.
It is easier for non-technical users to follow visually.
It shows the data stores used by each process.
It always uses less space when there are many conditions.
questions.explain: Key: B. A tree shows the logic as branches that the board members can trace without learning a Y/N/X grid. A is the most tempting distractor, but completeness is easier to check in a table, where the columns can be counted.

questions.stem: An analyst at Blue Channel Ferries in San Pedro is naming the process that sends each passenger a ticket after the card payment is authorised. Which of the following is a correctly named PROCESS?
questions.explain: Key: D. A process is named with a verb phrase describing the work done. "Booking request" (C) is a noun phrase suitable for a data flow, not a process.

questions.stem: A Lower Six student drawing the level 1 DFD for the Island Wheels Car Rentals must add the file that holds rental agreements. Which statement about this data store in Gane and Sarson notation is TRUE?
options: It is drawn as an open-ended rectangle and identified as D1, D2 or D3
It may receive data directly from the Customer entity
It must also appear on the context level DFD
It is drawn as a square and named with a verb
questions.explain: Key: A. The Rental Agreements store is an open-ended rectangle with a D-identifier. C is tempting, but stores are hidden inside process 0 at context level.

questions.stem: An algorithm for the Trinidad Taxi Co. contains the step "Repeat: drive to the next stop." with no stopping condition. This step violates which characteristic?
questions.explain: Key: B. With no stopping condition the algorithm never terminates. Option C is tempting, but the order of steps is clear; the problem is that it never ends.

questions.stem: A CAPE student in Georgetown, Guyana, is planning an algorithm that prices produce for a market stall and lists ways she could represent it. Which list contains ONLY ways of representing algorithms named in the CAPE IT syllabus?
questions.explain: Key: C. The syllabus names natural language, flowcharts and pseudocode. Option B is tempting because DFDs are diagrams, but a DFD models the flow of data through a system, not the steps of an algorithm.

questions.stem: For a Caribbean government's finance ministry, a team uses requirements gathering, design, version control, testing and planned maintenance to build a national tax-filing system over three years. This approach BEST describes
questions.explain: Key: A. A disciplined process for large, reliable software is Software Engineering. Computer Science is tempting because programming is involved, but CS focuses on theory and algorithms rather than the development process.

questions.stem: An employee at a Kingston hotel installs servers, configures the Wi-Fi network, manages user accounts and helps staff when devices fail. This role is MOST closely related to
questions.explain: Key: B. Deploying, administering and supporting infrastructure for users is Information Technology. Information Systems is tempting because the setting is an organisation, but IS focuses on processes and decisions rather than running the infrastructure.

questions.stem: At the Harbour View Internet Café in St. George’s, a tourist tells the owner, "The Internet and the Web are just two names for the same thing." Which statement CORRECTLY distinguishes the two?
options: The Web is the physical network; the Internet is a collection of pages.
The Internet is a global network of networks; the Web is a service of linked pages that runs on it.
The Web was created before the Internet.
They are two names for the same thing.
questions.explain: Key: B. The Internet (network, TCP/IP) existed before the Web (1989 to 1991), which is one service running on it, so the tourist is wrong. Option A reverses the two.

questions.stem: Engineers planning a new telecommunications link between St. Lucia and a neighbouring island choose fibre-optic cable rather than copper wire. They choose fibre MAINLY because fibre
options: is cheaper to lay on the seabed
carries much more data over long distances with less signal loss
works without electricity at either end
cannot be damaged by ships' anchors
questions.explain: Key: B. Light in glass fibre offers far higher bandwidth and lower loss than electrical signals in copper. Fibre cables can still be cut by anchors.

questions.stem: At Sandy Point Medical Centre, patients' test results may be seen only by authorised doctors, so the records are encrypted and protected by personal passwords. Which pair of characteristics of information is MOST concerned here?
questions.explain: Key: B. The rule that only authorised doctors may see results is confidentiality; encryption and passwords are the security controls that enforce it. Timeliness and lifespan concern when information is useful, not who may see it.

questions.stem: At Montego Bay Learning Centre, the exam registration system and the school office hold different dates of birth for the same student. This problem is BEST described as
questions.explain: Key: D. Two records of the same fact contradict each other: inconsistency. Distortion (C) is tempting, but it refers to meaning being changed as information is processed or passed on, not to two stored versions disagreeing.

questions.stem: A Lower Six student finds a journal article in which a team of researchers in Jamaica reviews and compares the findings of twenty earlier studies on mobile banking. As a source, this article is
options: a secondary source, because it analyses other people's research
a primary source, because it was published in a journal
a traditional source, because all journals are printed
a primary source, because it contains data
questions.explain: Key: A. A review article interprets and summarises earlier studies, so it is secondary. B is tempting, but the journal medium does not decide; an article reporting the team's own new survey would be primary.

questions.stem: During a storm a resident films live video of floodwater on Broad Street and posts it on social media. A week later a blogger writes a post comparing several such videos. Which statement about these sources is CORRECT?
options: The blog post is primary because it is the most recent source.
Both are secondary because all social media and blogs are secondary.
A source cannot be both electronic and primary, so the video must be secondary.
Whether a source is primary or secondary depends on its closeness to the original event, not its medium.
questions.explain: Key: D. The two classifications are independent: the live video is electronic and primary, while the blog post comparing videos is electronic and secondary. B is tempting, but a resident's own footage filmed during the event is first-hand, whatever the platform.

questions.stem: A Flamboyant Heights College student studying Internet access across the whole of Dominica finds a report that gives results for Roseau and Portsmouth but omits all other districts. For his study, the report fails mainly on
questions.explain: Key: D. Important parts needed for the purpose are missing, which is completeness. Bias would require a one-sided slant from an interest; nothing suggests that here.

questions.stem: Leon, a Flamboyant Heights College student, finds a 300-page report on hurricane damage to Broad Street shops, but it has no figures for Holetown, which his project needs. Which statement correctly applies depth and completeness to this report?
options: Depth is a criterion and completeness a characteristic, so the report fails on depth.
The report has great depth, but it is incomplete for Leon because the Holetown figures he needs are missing.
Depth applies only to print and completeness only to web sites, so neither applies.
Both mean the number of pages, so a 300-page report is complete.
questions.explain: Key: B. Depth is a characteristic (SO 1.5): the report is very detailed. Completeness is a criterion judged against the user's purpose (SO 1.6): it lacks what Leon needs. Option A reverses the two.

questions.stem: Head office of Sunrise Pharmacies chain in Castries receives each of its three branches' daily sales sheets and places them together in one folder for the week. The operation carried out is
questions.explain: Key: C. Bringing data from several branches together into one set is collating. Retrieving is tempting, but nothing is being taken out of storage; new data is being brought together.

questions.stem: Every Friday afternoon, the manager of the Seaside Pharmacy branch in Gros Islet emails the weekly sales report to head office in Castries. In the information processing cycle, this is an example of
questions.explain: Key: B. Sending information electronically from one place to another is transmitting (part of storing, retrieving and transmitting). Collating is tempting because head office may later combine the branch reports, but the act described is sending.

questions.stem: A Form 6 student at Calabash Point Secondary is making a revision card headed "Ways of representing DATA (SO 1.8)". Which of the following lists contains ONLY items that belong on that card?
questions.explain: Key: C. Character, string and numeric (with aural and visual) are the data representations. Text, tables, video, graphs, charts and signals are ways of representing information.
