questions.stem: A ship in Grand Anse flashes a lamp: short, short, short, long, long, long, short, short, short. The message is being represented using
questions.explain: Key: B. Short and long flashes are dots and dashes, here ... --- ... (SOS) in Morse Code. Binary also uses two states, but binary uses 0s and 1s with place values, not dots and dashes for letters.

questions.stem: The Island Yacht Club sends one email to a single club address, and the message is automatically delivered to the inboxes of all 300 members. Which tool is the club using?
questions.explain: Key: C. A mailing list delivers one message to every subscriber’s inbox. Option B, a discussion forum, is the most common confusion, but forum posts stay on a website that members must visit.

questions.stem: Caribe Marts group is training new staff in Basseterre on who uses each of its information systems. Which pairing of system and typical users should the trainer present as correct?
questions.explain: Key: D. A DSS supports managers and analysts making semi-structured decisions. A is tempting because engineers work in offices, but engineers and scientists are knowledge workers who use a KWS.

questions.stem: Calabash Point Secondary installs new computers and a new registration program, but forgets to connect the office computers to the server holding student records, so staff cannot open any student file. Which component of the information system is missing?
questions.explain: Key: C. The network connects hardware so that data can be shared. D is tempting because cables and routers are physical, but the question is about the missing communication link, which is the network component.

questions.stem: Portsmouth Market wants to print customer receipts quickly and quietly without buying ink or toner. Which printer is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Key: C. Thermal printers use heat-sensitive paper and no ink. A laser printer is fast and quiet but needs toner.

questions.stem: At the Coral Reef Hotel in Grand Anse, the air-conditioning system keeps a guest’s room at 22 °C. The compressor that switches on to cool the room when it gets too warm acts as the
questions.explain: Key: B. The compressor is an actuator: it turns the processor’s signal into physical action. The sensor is tempting because it is also part of the loop, but it measures the room temperature rather than changing it.

questions.stem: At the Sea View Hotel in Basseterre, the head of the restaurant department uses last quarter's sales figures and her own experience to set the next quarter's overtime budget. This decision is BEST classified as
questions.explain: Key: A. Data (sales figures) plus judgement (experience) makes it semi-structured, and a department head setting a quarterly budget works at the tactical level. B is tempting because a budget involves calculation, but the judgement element means it is not fully structured.

questions.stem: Driving along Bridge Street on a hot afternoon, the owner of the Bridge Street Bakery says "Turn on the air conditioning" and the car responds. Which pair of HCI types does this interaction involve?
questions.explain: Key: C. The input is spoken (speech) and in an everyday sentence (natural language). B is tempting because the instruction is a command, but a command line requires typed input in exact syntax at a prompt.

questions.stem: A taxi driver leaves the shaded rank at Norman Manley International Airport and his phone screen automatically becomes brighter in the midday sun. This is achieved through
questions.explain: Key: D. A light sensor detects ambient light and adjusts the display. A screen reader (A) converts text to speech and has nothing to do with brightness.

questions.stem: A Sint Maarten government website offers English, Dutch and Spanish versions and writes dates as "3 Apr 2026" so that residents and visitors from different countries read them correctly. This adapts the interface mainly for
questions.explain: Key: D. Language and date formats differ across cultures. Education (A) is tempting because language relates to reading, but the adaptation targets different languages and conventions, not literacy level.

questions.stem: Caribbean Union Bank wants a full mesh network directly linking its 6 offices in Antigua, Curaçao, Aruba, Jamaica, Barbados and Trinidad. How many links are required?
questions.explain: Key: B. n(n-1)/2 = 6 × 5 ÷ 2 = 15 links for the bank's six offices. D (30) forgets to divide by 2 and counts each link twice.

questions.stem: Managers of Coral Reef Resorts in Jamaica and Barbados hold a weekly live meeting over the network in which they see and hear each other at the same time. This is
questions.explain: Key: D. Live video and audio between the two resorts is videoconferencing. B (teleconferencing) is tempting but typically uses an audio link only, so the managers would not see each other.

questions.stem: A Form 6 student at Calabash Point Secondary is labelling a TCP/IP poster for the computer lab and must pair each layer with one protocol. Which pair correctly matches a TCP/IP layer with a protocol used at that layer?
questions.explain: Key: B. Ethernet operates at the Network Access layer, so this label is correct. "Internet: TCP" is tempting because of the name TCP/IP, but TCP is a Transport protocol and IP is the Internet protocol.

questions.stem: The owner of the Grand Anse Surf Shop sees "WPA3 (AES)" on her new router’s settings page and asks what AES means. AES, as used in WPA2 and WPA3, is BEST described as
options: a method of filtering MAC addresses
questions.explain: Key: A. AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) is the symmetric encryption algorithm that scrambles the surf shop’s Wi-Fi traffic inside WPA2 and WPA3. MAC filtering is tempting because it is another Wi-Fi setting, but it controls access, not encryption.

questions.stem: At Saba Dive Shop, the booking PC cannot get online. A technician pings the default gateway, 192.168.1.1, and receives "Request timed out" four times. Which conclusion is MOST reasonable?
options: There is a problem between the PC and the router, or the router is blocking ping.
The DNS server address is wrong.
The Internet speed is below the plan.
The website being visited is offline.
questions.explain: Key: A. The gateway is the shop's router, so no reply points to the PC-to-router link or a rule blocking ping. DNS is tempting, but pinging an IP address does not use DNS.

questions.stem: The administrator at the Bayside Family Clinic in Gros Islet wants only the clinic's registered laptops to join the staff Wi-Fi, even if a patient learns the network key. Which setting should be added?
questions.explain: Key: A. MAC filtering admits only devices whose hardware addresses are on the clinic's allow list. Hiding the SSID is tempting, but a patient who knows the name and key can still join.

questions.stem: After Hurricane Irma, the Harbour Insurance Agency in Road Town began keeping its backup drives in a fire-proof safe in a separate building in East End. This is BEST described as
questions.explain: Key: C. A fire-proof safe in another building physically protects the agency's backup drives. Logical access control is tempting because backups hold data, but the safe protects the drives themselves, not access through software.

questions.stem: A consultant is helping the Kingston Print Shop deal with a growing backlog of print jobs. Which of her activities is MOST closely associated with the "select and justify the optimal solution" stage?
options: Explaining why one system is better than the others in terms of cost and effectiveness
Training staff on the new job-tracking system
Interviewing staff to find the cause of the backlog
Listing three possible job-tracking systems with their costs
questions.explain: Key: A. Justifying means giving reasons for a choice by comparing it with the alternatives, as the consultant does when she explains why one system beats the others. D is tempting, but listing the systems with costs belongs to identifying and evaluating possible solutions.

questions.stem: Statia Dive Centre in Oranjestad sets up its chosen online booking system, enters its boats and timetables, and trains both staff members to use it. Which stage of the problem-solving process is this?
options: Select and justify the optimal solution
questions.explain: Key: B. Setting up the chosen system, entering data and training staff put the solution into action, which is implementation. D is tempting because it comes next, but evaluation and review happens after the system is running, when results are compared with the problem statement.

questions.stem: A student uses a health website from another country to plan a nutrition campaign in Jamaica, but the foods and eating habits described are uncommon there. Which criterion is the student MOST likely to have overlooked?
questions.explain: Key: B. The information was produced for a different society with different foods and habits. Accuracy is tempting, but the information may be correct for its original setting.

questions.stem: Mr. Lake, a CAPE IT teacher in Belize City, writes four revision flashcards on categories of information for his class. Which flashcard correctly matches the category with its definition?
options: Desirable: information that improves the solution but is not strictly required
Cosmetic: information that is irrelevant to the problem
Essential: information that improves the solution but is not required
Desirable: information without which the problem cannot be solved
questions.explain: Key: A. Desirable information adds value but the problem can still be solved without it. Option D describes essential information and Option B describes extraneous information.

questions.stem: Leeward Islands Pension Fund in Basseterre needs software to calculate pensions set by law. The requirements are fully known and stable, and an external auditor must review the documents from every stage. Which model is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: Key: C. Stable, fully known requirements and formal stage documentation suit Waterfall. Agile (B) is tempting as a modern model, but it values working software over comprehensive documentation and expects change.

questions.stem: A team building an app for the Saba Dive Centre works in two-week cycles, meets briefly every morning and has a customer representative who reorders a prioritised list of features before each cycle. Which model is being used?
questions.explain: Key: D. Time-boxed sprints, daily stand-ups and a product owner managing a backlog are Agile practices. Plan-driven incremental (A) is tempting because it also uses cycles, but it lacks the continuous customer collaboration and daily stand-ups.

questions.stem: San Pedro Hardware has compared an online-ordering package with a custom web store and must now give the owner a document recommending whether, and how, to proceed. Which deliverable is this?
questions.explain: Key: A. The feasibility study produces the system proposal recommending whether to proceed. A conversion plan (A) belongs to implementation, after the web store is built.

questions.stem: Four months after the Island Wheels Car Rentals booking system went live, the analyst counts double bookings and compares the figure with the target in the system proposal. Which BEST describes the SDLC stage she is carrying out?
options: Testing each program module with normal, boundary and erroneous data
Evaluating the live system against the objectives set in the system proposal
Training users and converting data to the new format
Investigating how the current manual system works
questions.explain: Key: B. Review evaluates the system after go-live against its objectives. A is testing during development, which happens before go-live.

questions.stem: The analyst for the Saba Dive Centre needs to understand why the owner schedules dive trips the way she does, and wants to respond at once to anything unclear she says. Which fact-finding tool gives the BEST opportunity to ask follow-up questions?
questions.explain: Key: D. In an interview with the owner, the analyst can respond to each answer immediately with further questions about her reasons. Observation (C) involves the analyst on site, but the analyst is watching rather than questioning.

questions.stem: Librarians and students at Mahoe Grove High School cannot clearly describe what they want the search screens of a proposed library system to look like, though they say they will "know it when they see it". Which tool would BEST help the analyst?
questions.explain: Key: B. A prototype lets users see and try the screens and react, which clarifies unclear requirements. An ER diagram (D) models stored data, not what the screens look like.

questions.stem: An analyst drawing a level 1 DFD for the Island Hardware store checks every arrow before showing the diagram to the owner. Which of the following data flows is ILLEGAL on the DFD?
options: From external entity Customer to data store D1
From process 1.0 to data store D1
From external entity Customer to process 1.0
From data store D2 to process 3.0
questions.explain: Key: A. A customer cannot write straight into the store; a process must be in between. Options B and D are legal because a process is at one end.

questions.stem: On the context level DFD for the Portsmouth Marine Services payroll in Roseau, the Bank receives payment details from the system each fortnight but sends nothing back. The Bank is BEST described as
questions.explain: Key: A. An external entity that only receives data is a sink. B is tempting because the Bank is an external entity, but a source sends data into the system.

questions.stem: A student's algorithm for the Gros Islet Laundromat gets the load weight, calculates the price and then displays it, and it is always clear which step comes next. It shows "flow of control from one process to another", which means that
options: the algorithm can be used by only one person at a time
every step must be a calculation
the algorithm must contain at least one decision
the steps are carried out in a clear, logical order with no doubt about which step comes next
questions.explain: Key: D. Flow of control is the order of execution and the passing of control from step to step. Option C is tempting because decisions affect the flow, but a simple sequence with no decision still has a flow of control.

questions.stem: An analyst at the Bridgetown firm CodeWave must present a refund algorithm with several decisions to a client in Barbados and is choosing between a flowchart and pseudocode. Which is an ADVANTAGE of the flowchart over pseudocode?
options: It is more compact for very large algorithms
It converts more directly into program code
It shows the flow of control and decision paths visually
questions.explain: Key: D. Arrows and diamonds make each refund decision and its paths visible at a glance. Option C is tempting, but pseudocode, not a flowchart, is closest to program code.

questions.stem: A Sixth Form student at Hummingbird Ridge High School is desk-checking a discount rule for Montego Bay Bakery: a ← 8; b ← 2; IF a - b * 3 > 3 THEN OUTPUT a / b ELSE OUTPUT a + b ENDIF. What is output?
questions.explain: Key: C. b * 3 = 6 first, then 8 − 6 = 2; 2 > 3 is FALSE, so the ELSE branch outputs 8 + 2 = 10. 4 is tempting if you work left to right: (8 − 2) * 3 = 18 > 3 would wrongly select the THEN branch and output 8 / 2.

questions.stem: At a careers evening at Flamboyant Heights College, a speaker says one word covers computer engineers, computer scientists, software engineers, IT specialists and IS analysts alike. Which term, the BROADEST of these, is she using?
questions.explain: Computing is the umbrella term covering every discipline the speaker listed. Computer Science is the most tempting distractor, but it is only one discipline within Computing.

questions.stem: At the firm Caribe Devices in Trinidad and Tobago, a specialist designs the circuit board and writes the firmware for a new card-payment terminal to be used in Regent Street shops. This work BEST represents
questions.explain: Designing the terminal's hardware and firmware is Computer Engineering. Software Engineering is tempting because firmware is software, but designing the circuit board places the work in CE.

questions.stem: Mrs Arrindell of English Harbour receives an APUA bill three times higher than usual. The clerk had keyed in her meter reading as 2,450 instead of 245. Which limitation of IT does this illustrate?
questions.explain: The system processed the wrong input exactly as given and produced a wrong bill: GIGO. Dependence on power is tempting because APUA supplies electricity, but the problem here is bad data, not an outage.

questions.stem: Nadia, an IT manager at a bank in Paramaribo, wants a professional title that shows employers she is a chartered IT practitioner. Which professional organisation awards the status she is looking for?
questions.explain: BCS, The Chartered Institute for IT, awards Chartered IT Professional (CITP) status, which is what Nadia wants. ACM is tempting as a large computing body, but it is known for the Digital Library and Turing Award, not chartership.

questions.stem: At Portsmouth Resort, Anya configures the servers, Wi-Fi and staff accounts, while Ravi studies how bookings are processed and designs reports that help managers decide on room prices. Which statement BEST distinguishes Ravi's discipline from Anya's?
options: Ravi's discipline is a branch of Computer Engineering; Anya's is a branch of Computer Science.
Ravi designs computer hardware; Anya designs algorithms.
Ravi works in IS, which focuses on how information and technology serve the resort's processes and decisions; Anya works in IT, which focuses on the technology infrastructure and its users.
Ravi and Anya work in the same discipline under two different names.
questions.explain: Ravi starts from the organisation (IS); Anya starts from the infrastructure (IT). Treating them as one discipline is the commonest misconception, but their focus and roles differ.

questions.stem: At Little Bay Computer Museum, a display card reads: "This 1965 machine was built with many transistors formed together on small silicon chips, but it had no CPU on a single chip." Which generation does the card describe?
questions.explain: Many transistors on one chip is an integrated circuit, which defines the third generation (1964 to 1971). The fourth generation is tempting, but the card says there is no CPU on one chip, and that is what a microprocessor is.

questions.stem: In a Frangipani Hill Academy lesson, the teacher shows a video of a Jacquard loom (1804) weaving a pattern controlled by a chain of punched cards, and asks why this loom matters in the history of computing. The BEST answer is that it
options: could add numbers using geared wheels
was the first machine to use binary electronics
used punched cards to store a changeable set of instructions
questions.explain: Swapping the cards in the video changes the pattern: an early stored, changeable set of instructions. Geared addition describes the Pascaline, not the loom.

questions.stem: A technician at the Leeward Motors garage in Jolly Harbour works with four computer systems in one day. Which of them is the BEST example of an embedded computer?
options: The controller in a customer's car anti-lock braking system
The laptop she uses to look up repair manuals
The airline mainframe that books her holiday flight
The desktop PC in the garage office
questions.explain: The braking controller is built into the car to do one dedicated task: embedded. The laptop and office desktop are microcomputers, general-purpose machines for one user.

questions.stem: For a Coralstone College open-day poster, a student has four cards: I. TCP/IP adopted by ARPANET  II. World Wide Web created  III. ARPANET launched  IV. Network email sent. In which order should the cards go, earliest first?
questions.explain: ARPANET (1969), email (1971), TCP/IP (1983), Web (1989 to 1991). Putting the Web before TCP/IP is the tempting error: the Web runs on an Internet that already existed.

questions.stem: A grandmother in Paramaribo remembers that her mobile phone in the late 1990s was the first one that gave her clear digital calls and let her send SMS text messages. Which mobile generation was that phone?
questions.explain: 2G (GSM, from 1991) was the first digital mobile standard and brought SMS. 1G was analogue voice only; 3G added mobile data, which her phone is not described as having.

questions.stem: At the Seaside Pharmacy in Belmopan, a new clerk finds a box of old till rolls showing amounts such as 12.50, 4.75 and 30.00, with no dates or product names. What the clerk has found is BEST described as
options: knowledge, because the amounts can be used to make decisions
information, because the amounts have been processed to give them meaning
data, because they are raw, unorganised facts with little meaning on their own
a report, because the amounts were printed by a computer system
questions.explain: The amounts are raw, unprocessed and unorganised, with no context, so they are data. Option B is the most tempting distractor, but nothing has been totalled, sorted or put in context, so they are not yet information.

questions.stem: Portsmouth Sands Hotel asks departing guests to rate their room from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent) on a tablet in the lobby. The ratings collected are BEST described as
options: detailed, because every guest is asked
information, because they have been processed
questions.explain: The numbers record subjective opinions, so the data is qualitative. Option C is tempting because the values are numbers, but they are not objective measurements.

questions.stem: At Mahoe Grove High School in Barbados, the term attendance report reaches form teachers two weeks after term ends, too late to contact the parents of absent students. Which characteristic of information is MOST affected?
questions.explain: Information that arrives after it is needed fails on timeliness. Shareability is tempting because the report is distributed, but it was shared; it was simply late.

questions.stem: Georgetown Transit Office reviews rainfall records each evening before planning the next day's bus routes. Which statement in its planning notes represents knowledge?
options: Rainfall last month was double the average.
Heavy rain usually floods the low road, so buses will use the hill route tomorrow.
questions.explain: Knowledge uses information and experience to make a decision: the office knows heavy rain floods the low road and therefore reroutes the buses. Option A is tempting because it is processed and meaningful, but it is information: no decision is made.

questions.stem: San Pedro Catering Company uses an accurate, carefully checked list of last year's cruise-ship arrivals at the Belize City cruise port to plan staffing for a new school canteen. The MAIN weakness of this data is that it is
questions.explain: Accurate data can still be the wrong data for a decision: this is appropriateness. Option B is tempting, but the list is described as accurate, so quality is not the issue.

questions.stem: Jaden, a student at Breadfruit Valley Secondary, is gathering material for a project on Hurricane Irma in 2017. Which item in his folder is a PRIMARY source?
options: A video recorded by a resident of The Valley during Hurricane Irma
An encyclopaedia entry on Hurricane Irma
A magazine review of a documentary about the hurricane
A textbook chapter on Caribbean history
questions.explain: The resident's video is original, first-hand evidence made at the time of the storm. The encyclopaedia entry is tempting because it is about the same event, but it summarises other sources, so it is secondary.

questions.stem: The IT department at Sandbox Tree College in Barbados wants an online space where all its teachers can write and correct the same revision notes together. Which feature MOST clearly makes a wiki a better choice than a blog for this?
options: A wiki contains images and hyperlinks.
A wiki is published on the World Wide Web.
A wiki allows readers to post comments.
Many users can edit the same pages of a wiki.
questions.explain: Collaborative editing by many users is the defining feature of a wiki, which is exactly what the teachers need. Option C is tempting, but comments are typical of blogs; on a blog readers comment but cannot edit the post.

questions.stem: Marisol, an Upper Six student in Basseterre, is writing a report on the smartphone features released this year. A disadvantage of using a printed library book rather than a manufacturer's web site is that the book
options: is likely to be out of date
questions.explain: Books take months or years to produce, so for this year's smartphones Marisol's book will have dated. "Can be edited by anyone" is tempting because it is a known weakness of some sources, but it applies to wikis, not books.

questions.stem: A Sandbox Tree College student researching coastal erosion in Anguilla can use her library's electronic database of journal articles or a general web search. Which is the MAIN advantage of the database for her?
options: Its content is selected and can be searched precisely with filters.
It is always free to the public.
It works without an Internet connection.
questions.explain: Selected, quality content and precise, filtered searching let her find published research on Anguilla quickly. "Always free" is tempting because she uses it through her library at no charge, but many databases require paid subscriptions.

questions.stem: During a tropical storm, residents of Gros Islet share many posts about flooded roads on social media, and a driver uses them to plan his route. Which is the MOST significant disadvantage of relying on these posts?
options: They are always out of date.
They can only be read on a CD-ROM.
They may contain rumours that have not been checked.
questions.explain: Social media lacks editorial checking, so the driver may act on rumours or old photos. "Always out of date" is tempting as a general weakness, but social media is actually one of the most current sources.

questions.stem: Nadia, a CAPE student in Arnos Vale, is making notes on a general encyclopaedia entry about the Caribbean that covers every island in a few lines each. Which of her note headings names a CHARACTERISTIC of the source rather than a criterion for selecting it?
questions.explain: Breadth of coverage describes the source (SO 1.5): the entry covers many islands. Bias, cultural context and completeness are tests for selection (SO 1.6). Completeness is the most tempting distractor because it sounds like depth or breadth, but it judges the source against the user's needs.

questions.stem: A student in Georgetown revises for a history test by listening to a podcast episode about Caribbean history, streamed through a mobile app on her phone. Which pair correctly identifies its format and medium?
questions.explain: Audio is how the information is arranged (format); the app is the carrier (medium). Option A reverses them, the most common error.

questions.stem: A student finds that a usually trustworthy newspaper gave the wrong date for a hurricane in one article. Which criterion has the article failed?
questions.explain: A specific error fails the accuracy criterion. Reliability is tempting, but it describes the newspaper's general trustworthiness, which can remain high even when one article contains a mistake.

questions.stem: A Flamboyant Heights College lecturer tells her class that an article on coral health in San Pedro Lagoon comes from a refereed journal. Which statement about this article is TRUE?
options: It was reviewed by independent experts before publication.
It must be free and available online.
It is certain to be more current than a blog on the lagoon.
It was checked only by the publisher’s own editor.
questions.explain: Refereeing means independent expert review before publication. Editorial checking (option D) is a different, weaker form of quality control; refereed sources are often slower, so less current than blogs.

questions.stem: An Antigua business owner uses a US web site to learn about employee leave entitlements. Which criterion is MOST likely to make this source unsuitable?
questions.explain: Employment law differs between countries, so the source was produced for a different legal and cultural setting. Format, cost and depth are characteristics and do not address the mismatch.

questions.stem: A Year 12 student at Mahoe Grove High School in Antigua is drawing the information processing cycle on a revision poster, using the Seaside Pharmacy's weekly sales as the example. Which sequence should the poster show?
options: Processing, input, storage, output, with feedback to output
Output, processing, input, storage, with feedback to processing
Input, processing, output, storage, with optional feedback to input
Input, storage, output, processing, with compulsory feedback
questions.explain: The pharmacy's sales are entered (input), totalled and sorted (processing), reported (output) and saved (storage), and feedback is optional and loops back to input. The most tempting distractor sends feedback to output, but feedback evaluates the output and returns changes to the input stage.

questions.stem: At the Harbour View Supermarket in Roseau, the cashier passes each item over a scanner that reads its barcode, and the product name and price appear on the screen at once. This is an example of
questions.explain: The scanner reads the code directly from the product at the point of sale, which is automated data capture. "Manual data entry" is tempting because the cashier is involved, but she does not key or write the data; the device reads it.

questions.stem: The Year 13 form tutor at Coralstone College already has each student's average mark in a spreadsheet and now arranges the class list from the highest average to the lowest. Which processing operation is this?
questions.explain: Arranging records in order of a key field (average mark, descending) is sorting. Calculating is tempting because averages are involved, but the tutor already has the averages; the operation described is putting them in order.

questions.stem: Grand Anse Clinic keeps its patient folders in a manual filing system, filed alphabetically by surname. Which request would be MOST difficult for the clerk to satisfy?
options: Finding a folder for a given surname
Adding a new folder in the correct place
Finding all records for patients living in one district
questions.explain: District is not the clinic's filing key, so every folder must be checked. The other tasks all use the surname key. This is the main retrieval advantage of an automated system, which can search by any field.

questions.stem: Gros Islet Marina has replaced its paper berth register with a computerised booking system. Which of the following is a DISADVANTAGE of the new automated system compared with the old manual one?
options: It allows data to be sorted in any order
It depends on electricity and working equipment
It is slower with large volumes of data
questions.explain: The marina's new system needs power, equipment and often a network, so it can stop during outages such as after a hurricane, whereas the paper register kept working. "More calculation errors" is a misconception: computers calculate consistently if the input and program are correct.

questions.stem: A school database stores a student ID such as 004512. Which data type is MOST appropriate, and why?
options: Character, because each digit is a separate symbol
Numeric, because it is made up of digits
String, because it is not used in calculations and leading zeros must be kept
Visual, because it is printed on an ID card
questions.explain: IDs are never used in arithmetic, and storing them as numbers would drop the leading zeros, so a string is correct. Numeric is the tempting distractor because the ID contains only digits, but containing digits is not the test; being used in calculations is.

questions.stem: Calypso Corner music shop in Castries sells old vinyl records and MP3 downloads, texts customers about new stock and runs its till over fibre broadband. Which of these is an example of an analogue representation?
options: The groove on a vinyl record
Light pulses in the shop's fibre-optic cable
A text message sent over a mobile network
An MP3 file stored on a customer's phone
questions.explain: The vinyl groove is a continuous physical copy of the sound wave, so it is analogue. Fibre-optic pulses are tempting because light is involved, but the pulses are on/off states representing 1s and 0s, which is digital.

questions.stem: The computer at the San Fernando Marina stores the number of boats in the lagoon as the byte 10010110. How many boats are in the lagoon?
questions.explain: 128 + 16 + 4 + 2 = 150 boats. 105 comes from reading the bits in reverse (01101001), a common error when students write the place values from left to right in the wrong order.

questions.stem: A Coralstone College student opens a text file in a program that shows each character's ASCII code in denary. The upper-case letter H appears as 72. What code will she see for the upper-case letter L?
questions.explain: Letters are consecutive and L is four letters after H, so 72 + 4 = 76. 108 is tempting, but it is the code for lower-case l (76 + 32); the question asks for upper case.

questions.stem: During a steel pan rehearsal at Sea-Almond Secondary School, the music teacher writes a ♭ symbol before a note on the stave so the band plays it lower. This is an example of
questions.explain: The flat sign is a musical symbol that lowers a note by a semitone. Mathematical notation is the tempting distractor because both use symbols, but the stave and the flat sign belong only to music.

questions.stem: Coral Reef Bakery in Salem has a box between its computer and the telephone line. When the owner emails an order to a supplier, the box changes the data before it travels down the line. Which function is this modem performing?
options: Converting digital data into a signal for transmission and converting received signals back to digital data
Storing web pages so that they load faster
Directing data packets between several different networks
Finding web pages that match a user’s keywords
questions.explain: The bakery’s modem modulates outgoing data and demodulates incoming signals. The most tempting distractor is directing packets between networks, which is the job of a router.

questions.stem: Paramaribo Volleyball League uses several tools to communicate with its players and coaches. Which pair of the league’s tools are BOTH asynchronous?
options: A telnet session on the league’s server and a VoIP call
A VoIP call with the head coach and a web-conference team meeting
A mailing list for fixtures and a discussion forum for players’ questions
A web-conference team meeting and a mailing list for fixtures
questions.explain: The mailing list and the forum both store messages for players to read later. Option D is tempting because the mailing list is asynchronous, but the web-conference meeting is real-time.

questions.stem: A Form 6 student in Roseau uses an FTP client to copy a large folder of past-paper files from her school’s file server to her laptop so she can revise offline at home. This is called
questions.explain: The files move from the server to her laptop, so she is downloading. Uploading, the tempting distractor, is the opposite direction: from her laptop to the server.

questions.stem: The IT technician at the Bayside Clinic in Frigate Bay still uses telnet to log in to a server at the clinic’s branch in Sandy Point. A consultant advises replacing it with SSH. What is the MAIN reason for this advice?
options: It sends usernames and passwords as plain text.
It cannot work over the Internet.
questions.explain: Telnet’s plain-text transmission would expose the technician’s login details to anyone intercepting the traffic. "Can only transfer files" is a misunderstanding: file transfer is FTP’s job; telnet provides remote command-line login.

questions.stem: The principal of a primary school in Montego Bay must warn parents today about a sudden water shut-off. Many parents have only basic mobile phones without data plans. Which tool is MOST appropriate?
questions.explain: SMS works over the cellular network on any phone, so every parent receives the warning. A cross-platform messaging tool is tempting because it is popular, but it needs a smartphone app and Internet access that these parents lack.

questions.stem: Every Monday, the store manager of the Bayview Supermarket in Grand Anse automatically receives a short list of ONLY the products that sold below their weekly target. Which type of information system is MOST likely producing this report?
questions.explain: A scheduled exception report for a middle manager such as Bayview's store manager is MIS output. The TPS is tempting because it holds the underlying sales data, but it outputs processed transactions and detailed reports, not exception reports for managers.

questions.stem: At the Seaside Pharmacy in Montego Bay, a counter assistant rings up a bottle of sunscreen; the till prints a receipt and the stock file is reduced by one. Which of the following BEST describes the major OUTPUT of this Transaction Processing System?
questions.explain: The receipt and the reduced stock record are processed transactions, the typical TPS output. What-if forecasts are tempting because they also draw on transaction data, but they are produced by a DSS.

questions.stem: An architect in Frigate Bay uses CAD software on a powerful workstation to design and simulate a hurricane-resistant school building. This is an example of a(n)
questions.explain: A KWS helps knowledge workers create designs and models. OAS is tempting because both support office-based professionals, but an OAS handles documents, email and scheduling, not design and simulation.

questions.stem: At Island Breeze Hotel, a laminated card beside each front-desk computer lists the steps staff must follow to check in a guest and to back up the day's bookings. Which component of the information system does this card represent?
questions.explain: The card gives instructions for people, so it represents procedures. Software is the tempting distractor because it is also a set of instructions, but software instructs the hardware, not the front-desk staff.

questions.stem: A manager at a St. George’s bank suddenly asks for the number of loans issued to small businesses in Grand Anse during the last two hurricane seasons. The report produced is BEST described as
questions.explain: A one-off, unscheduled question answered on request produces an ad hoc report. A summarised report is tempting because the answer is a total, but summarised reports are routine and scheduled rather than produced for a sudden, specific question.

questions.stem: A bank in Barbados processes thousands of cheques daily. Which input method reads the account numbers printed along the bottom of each cheque?
questions.explain: Cheque numbers are printed in magnetic ink and read by MICR. OCR is tempting because it also reads characters, but it reads ordinary print optically, not magnetic ink.

questions.stem: At the Sunset Supermarket in San Pedro, the till program checks whether a customer’s loyalty points are greater than 500 before it gives a discount. Which part of the CPU carries out this comparison?
questions.explain: The ALU performs logical operations such as comparing the points total with 500. The control unit is tempting because it directs the process, but it fetches, decodes and coordinates rather than carrying out the comparison.

questions.stem: A Sandbox Tree College student is typing her Communication Studies essay when a power cut switches off her desktop. When the power returns, her unsaved work has gone because it was held in
options: the hard disk, which is volatile
questions.explain: Her unsaved essay sat in RAM, which loses its contents without power. The hard disk option is tempting but wrong: hard disks are non-volatile, which is why saved work survives a power cut.

questions.stem: A developer at the Philipsburg Software House has finished a booking program for a dive shop in Saba and wants to hand over one fast-running executable file. Which translator converts the entire high-level program into that file before it is run?
questions.explain: A compiler translates the whole program at once into an executable the dive shop can run. An interpreter is the tempting distractor, but it translates and runs one statement at a time and produces no executable.

questions.stem: Sensors on a river in Guyana record water levels and display them on a screen at the regional office, where staff decide whether to issue flood warnings. This is BEST described as
questions.explain: The system records and displays readings while staff decide what to do: monitoring. It is not control because no actuator changes the river or the process automatically.

questions.stem: The managers of the Harbourside Trading company in St. George’s face several decisions in the weeks after a major hurricane damages its head office. Which of these decisions is MOST likely to be unstructured?
options: Reordering printer paper when fewer than ten boxes remain
Calculating the turnover tax on a customer's bill
Deciding whether the company should move its head office to another island
Choosing which of two approved couriers to use for a routine delivery
questions.explain: Moving Harbourside's head office to another island is novel, uncertain and has no agreed procedure, so it is unstructured. Option D is tempting because it involves a choice, but both couriers are pre-approved and the decision is routine, so it is at most semi-structured.

questions.stem: Each morning, the shift supervisor at Island Fresh supermarket in Holetown checks a list of every item sold yesterday and today's stock count for each shelf. This operational information is BEST described as
options: periodic and compared with the budget
approximate and gathered only when needed
questions.explain: The supervisor's item-by-item sales list and shelf counts are detailed, internal and current, which is what operational staff need for daily tasks. Option A is tempting but describes tactical information, such as the store manager's monthly budget report.

questions.stem: A secretary at the Fort Street Law Office in Basseterre deletes an old letter by dragging its icon onto the recycle bin and watching it disappear at once. This is an example of
questions.explain: The secretary acts physically on a visible object (the letter's icon) and gets immediate feedback, which is direct manipulation. A menu is tempting because the action happens inside a GUI, but no list of options was selected.

questions.stem: At the Sunset Car Rental in Holetown, the cars respond only to the spoken phrases "Radio on" and "Call office", while the company website's chatbot answers typed questions such as "can I drop the car off at the airport?". Which statement BEST distinguishes the two interfaces?
options: A speech interface accepts spoken input, whereas a natural language interface accepts everyday sentences that may be typed or spoken.
A speech interface understands any sentence, whereas a natural language interface accepts only fixed commands.
Speech interfaces need a screen, whereas natural language interfaces do not.
Speech interfaces are used only in cars, whereas natural language interfaces are used only on websites.
questions.explain: The cars use speech (the voice channel); the chatbot uses natural language (everyday sentences, here typed). Option D is tempting because of where Sunset uses each one, but location does not define an interface. Option B reverses the truth: the cars' speech system accepts only fixed phrases.

questions.stem: An experienced network technician at Sandbox Tree College must apply the same settings to all 60 classroom computers before lessons start tomorrow. Which type of HCI is MOST suitable for this task?
questions.explain: A command line lets an expert type or script commands to repeat a task quickly with precise control. A menu is tempting because it is easy to use, but stepping through menus 60 times is slow for an expert.

questions.stem: Caribbean Credit Union's new teller system must suit staff with 15 years' experience and new hires starting next week. Which pair of HCI evaluation principles is MOST likely to conflict in this design?
options: Use of colour and ease of navigation
Ease of use and ease of learning
questions.explain: The experienced tellers want fast, efficient interaction (ease of use) such as shortcuts, while the new hires need guided, learnable steps (ease of learning), which can slow the experts down. Alignment and colour are tempting because both are visual, but they usually support each other rather than conflict.

questions.stem: On the Philipsburg Ferry Co. website, the menu appears in a different position on every page and there is no Home link, so tourists booking trips to Saba keep getting lost. Which principle is MOST affected?
questions.explain: Tourists cannot reliably find their way or return home, which is navigation. Alignment is tempting because the menu "moves", but the main effect on the tourists is getting lost, not an untidy layout.

questions.stem: At the Island Health Clinic in English Harbour, four people work with the patient records system every day. Which of them is an end user rather than an IT professional?
options: The database administrator who backs up the records
The help-desk technician who fixes staff log-in problems
The programmer who writes updates to the system
The nurse who enters patient notes during appointments
questions.explain: The nurse uses the system to do her own job. The help-desk technician is tempting because they also "help users", but supporting the system is an IT professional role.

questions.stem: A clerk at a Bartica law firm has severe arthritis in both hands and cannot use a mouse or keyboard for long. Which adaptation BEST supports her?
questions.explain: Voice control removes the need to use a mouse or keyboard. High contrast is tempting as a common accessibility feature, but it supports vision, not mobility.

questions.stem: An ATM on Fort Street, Basseterre has a raised dot on the number 5 key and offers audio guidance through a headphone jack so that blind customers can withdraw cash. These are examples of
questions.explain: Touch markers and audio let blind customers interact without seeing the screen. Sensors is tempting, but a sensor detects physical changes as input; the dot and audio are tactile and audio interfaces.

questions.stem: The IT technician at Mahoe Grove High School needs a device that links the school LAN to the Internet service and forwards packets between the two networks using IP addresses. Which device should she install?
questions.explain: A router connects different networks, here the school LAN and the Internet, and forwards packets by IP address. A switch is tempting but it works within one LAN using MAC addresses.

questions.stem: Staff at the Island Hotel Group log in to a private web portal to read rosters and policies. Guests and suppliers cannot reach it at all. This portal is
questions.explain: The portal uses web technologies but is private and staff-only, so it is an intranet. An extranet is tempting, but it would open access to authorised outsiders such as the suppliers.

questions.stem: At Young Street Jewellers, one PC's cable is cut and only that PC goes offline. A week later the central device fails and every PC loses its connection. Which topology does the shop use?
questions.explain: In a star each PC has its own cable, so one cut affects one PC, but the central switch is a single point of failure. Bus is tempting, but a cut in a bus backbone would stop the whole shop network at once.

questions.stem: Two security guards at the Castries cruise port use handheld radios: one presses a button to talk while the other must wait to listen, then they swap. This is an example of
questions.explain: Data flows in both directions but only one at a time, so the guards' radios are half duplex. Simplex is tempting, but in simplex the receiver can never reply.

questions.stem: English Harbour Boatyard must link its office to a workshop that sits beside heavy welding machinery producing strong electrical interference. Which transmission medium is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: Fibre carries light, so the welding machinery's electrical interference cannot affect it. Coaxial is tempting because it is shielded, but it still carries electrical signals and is not immune.

questions.stem: Before a photo leaves a student's phone at St. John’s College, it is compressed to JPEG and encrypted so that only the receiver can read it. At which layer of the OSI model are this encryption and compression performed?
questions.explain: Compressing and encrypting the photo changes the format of the data, which is the Presentation layer’s job (translation, encryption and compression). Session is the tempting distractor, but it manages dialogue (opening, managing and closing conversations), not format.

questions.stem: A tourist at the Bridgetown cruise pier opens a website hosted in Miami. Routers along the way read each packet’s IP address and choose a path between networks. Which TCP/IP layer is responsible for this logical addressing and routing?
questions.explain: The Internet layer uses IP addresses to route the tourist’s packets between networks. Transport is tempting because it also deals with delivery, but it handles end-to-end delivery between programs using ports, not routing.

questions.stem: In the computer lab at Palmetto Point Secondary, a network device learns the MAC addresses of the 20 connected PCs and forwards each frame only to the intended PC. This device is a
questions.explain: A switch works at Layer 2 with MAC addresses and forwards each frame to one port, as in the lab. A router is tempting, but it forwards packets between networks using IP addresses.

questions.stem: Pelican Key Villas are comparing four ways to protect the guest Wi-Fi at their rental units. Which of the following provides the STRONGEST protection for the wireless network?
options: WPA3 with a long network key
questions.explain: WPA3 uses AES encryption with the SAE handshake, and a long key resists guessing, so the villas’ traffic is protected. MAC filtering is tempting, but MAC addresses can be spoofed and it does not encrypt traffic.

questions.stem: A student is designing a network for Portsmouth Dental Clinic and must protect the reception PC, the dentist's PC and the patient-records server from Internet attacks. Where should the firewall be placed on the diagram?
options: Between the router (WAN side) and the switch (LAN side)
After the wireless access point only
Between one PC and the switch
questions.explain: Placing the firewall at the WAN–LAN boundary means all traffic entering or leaving the clinic LAN is filtered, protecting every device. Placing it before one PC is tempting but protects only that PC.

questions.stem: At the Harbour View Insurance office in Belize City, a newly installed PC cannot open any website. Its ipconfig output shows IPv4 Address 169.254.40.12 and no default gateway. What does this MOST likely indicate?
options: The DNS server is not responding
The PC did not receive an address from a DHCP server
The firewall is blocking web traffic
The PC has a static IP address set correctly
questions.explain: A 169.254 address is self-assigned when no DHCP server replies, and the new PC has no gateway. DNS failure is tempting, but a DNS fault would still show a normal address and gateway; the problem here is at the addressing stage.

questions.stem: Sunset Café near the Roseau cruise pier gives its Wi-Fi password to every customer. Which setting stops a customer who knows that password from changing the router's configuration?
questions.explain: The router password protects the management settings. The network key is tempting, but it only lets devices join the Wi-Fi, and the café's customers already know it.

questions.stem: A clerk at the Island Hop Travel agency in St. George’s can ping 8.8.8.8 successfully but cannot open www.example.com by name. The fault is MOST likely with
questions.explain: Replies from a public IP prove the clerk's cable, gateway and Internet path work, so only name resolution is failing. The gateway is tempting, but traffic to 8.8.8.8 passes through it successfully.

questions.stem: In an old lab at Portsmouth Learning Centre, every PC taps into one main cable with a terminator at each end. A chair crushes that cable and every PC loses its connection. Which topology does the lab use?
questions.explain: All bus devices share one backbone, so the crushed cable stops the whole lab network. Star is tempting because the central device is a single point of failure, but a cable break in a star affects only one device.

questions.stem: St. Kitts Seaview Hotel must link its reception block to a villa 600 m away, along a route past the laundry's heavy machinery. Which statement BEST compares fibre-optic cable with twisted-pair Ethernet for this link?
options: Twisted pair is more secure than fibre because it uses electricity.
Fibre is cheaper and easier to install than twisted pair.
Fibre carries data further and is immune to electrical interference, whereas twisted pair is limited to about 100 m per run.
Both media are affected equally by electrical interference.
questions.explain: Fibre uses light, so it covers the 600 m and ignores the laundry's electrical noise; twisted-pair runs are limited to about 100 m. Option B is tempting because fibre is widely installed, but fibre is generally more expensive and harder to terminate.

questions.stem: Frigate Bay Marina Hotel is listing its security measures for an insurance inspector. Which of the following measures on the list is a LOGICAL access control measure?
options: Read-only access rights for junior clerks
A security guard at the main entrance
A cable lock on a laptop
questions.explain: Access rights are set in the hotel's software and control what clerks can do with data, so they are logical. A security guard is tempting because guards control access, but they control entry to a building, which is physical.

questions.stem: The IT officer at the Sandy Ground Shipping Agency asks four new clerks to suggest passwords for the cargo database. Which suggestion BEST meets all the characteristics of an effective password?
questions.explain: R3d!KiteOver7Bays has well over eight characters, upper and lower case, numbers, a special character in fourth place and nothing personal. "mypassword2024" is tempting because it is long and alphanumeric, but it is obvious and has no upper-case letters and no special character.

questions.stem: To enter the baggage-handling control room at the John A. Osborne Airport Ground Services office, a supervisor presents her staff card and then places her finger on a scanner. This is an example of
options: two-factor authentication using something you have and something you are
questions.explain: The supervisor's card is something she has and her fingerprint is something she is: two different factors. "Single-factor using two devices" is tempting, but what counts is the number of different factor types, not the number of devices.

questions.stem: On Monday morning the Holetown Car Rentals finds that its bookings file will not open. Which of the following events from the weekend is the MOST likely cause of this data corruption?
options: A file being encrypted with a strong key
A clerk being given read-only access
A sudden power cut while a file is being saved
questions.explain: A save interrupted by a power cut can leave the bookings file partly written and unreadable. Encryption is tempting because ciphertext looks unreadable, but it is deliberate and reversible with the key, so it is not corruption.

questions.stem: A customer pays the Domineestraat Electronics online store by card. Anyone intercepting the payment on the café Wi-Fi sees only a jumble of characters. This scrambled, unreadable form of the data is called
questions.explain: Ciphertext is the output of encryption. Plaintext is tempting because it is the other half of the pair, but plaintext is the readable data before encryption.

questions.stem: A Lower Sixth student at Palmetto Point Secondary says: "When the island's undersea cable was damaged, the World Wide Web went down, so the Internet and the web must be the same thing." Which statement BEST describes the relationship between the Internet and the World Wide Web?
options: The Internet and the World Wide Web are two names for the same network.
The World Wide Web is a service of linked hypertext documents that runs on the Internet.
The Internet is a collection of web pages stored on the World Wide Web.
The World Wide Web is the hardware that connects networks together.
questions.explain: The cable is part of the Internet (the network); the web is one service that depends on it, so it fails too, but they are not the same thing. Option C, the most tempting distractor, reverses the relationship.

questions.stem: Sasha, a student at Coralstone College in Dominica, is sent the link https://www.example.dm/news/today.html for a class article about the Roseau cruise season. In this URL, which part is the path?
questions.explain: /news/ is the folder (path) on the server. today.html is the file name, which candidates often confuse with the path.

questions.stem: Carenage Snorkel Tours site shows a beach photo, beach.jpg. The owner wants the words "Carenage beach" to appear if the photo cannot load and to be read aloud by screen readers. Which HTML is correct?
options: img src="beach.jpg" alt="Carenage beach" (in angle brackets)
img href="beach.jpg" alt="Carenage beach" (in angle brackets)
img src="beach.jpg" title="Carenage beach" (in angle brackets)
img src="Carenage beach" alt="beach.jpg" (in angle brackets)
questions.explain: src gives the file and alt gives the text shown if it fails and read by screen readers. Option C uses title, which is only a hover tooltip, not replacement text.

questions.stem: Kingston Tutoring Centre is building an online registration form. Each student must choose exactly ONE of three subjects: Mathematics, Physics or Information Technology. Which form control is MOST appropriate?
options: Radio buttons with the same name
questions.explain: Radio buttons sharing a name allow only one selection, so each student gets exactly one subject. Checkboxes are tempting but would let a student tick all three.

questions.stem: A guest at a Grand Anse hotel types www.example.gd into her laptop. Before her browser can request the page, the Domain Name System carries out domain name resolution. This process
options: converts the domain name into an IP address
loads the home page of the web site
converts HTML into XML for transport
registers a new domain name with a registrar
questions.explain: DNS resolution maps the name she typed to the server's IP address so the browser knows where to send its HTTP request. Registering a domain (C) is a different process that the site owner completes long before any guest visits.

questions.stem: At a staff meeting, the manager of the Gros Islet Bakery says: "We will fix our lost-orders problem by defining it, analysing it, comparing options, choosing one, putting it in place and checking the results." Which of the following BEST describes what the manager is planning?
options: A process of finding solutions to a problem by following ordered stages
Writing a computer program to automate the order book
Removing the symptoms of the problem as quickly as possible
questions.explain: The manager describes ordered stages from defining the problem to checking the results, which matches the syllabus description of problem-solving as a process of finding solutions. Writing a program is tempting because this is an IT course, but a program is only one possible solution, and the manager has not chosen one yet.

questions.stem: The committee of the Harbourside Craft Market has agreed a problem statement, found that stock-outs happen because sales are never totalled, and listed its budget limit. Which stage should the committee carry out NEXT?
options: Select and justify the optimal solution
questions.explain: The committee has finished defining and analysing, so it must now identify and evaluate possible solutions. "Select and justify" is tempting, but it cannot select the optimal solution until alternatives have been identified and evaluated.

questions.stem: A student at Bayleaf Hill Secondary is writing a problem statement for a Mesopotamia farmer whose sweet peppers are being attacked by whitefly. Which should the statement include? I. Who or what is affected II. How they are affected III. The consequence if the problem is not fixed IV. The pesticide to be used
questions.explain: The farmer's problem statement should say who/what is affected (her sweet peppers), how (whitefly damage) and the consequence. Including IV is tempting, but naming the pesticide puts a solution into the statement and closes off other options such as traps or netting.

questions.stem: The owner of the Seaside Pharmacy in Gros Islet notes that she can spend no more than EC$135 a month and that her two pharmacists have only basic computer skills. During which stage is she identifying these limits?
questions.explain: The US$50 budget and the pharmacists' skills are constraints, and constraints are identified during analysis. "Define the problem" is tempting, but definition states what the problem is and who it affects, not the limits on solutions.

questions.stem: Palmetto Point Secondary installs a new library booking system and, three months later, compares the number of lost books with the figure recorded before the change. This activity is part of which stage?
options: Select and justify the optimal solution
questions.explain: Comparing results with the original problem after the solution is in use is evaluation and review. "Implement" is tempting because the system was installed, but measuring its effect is a separate, later stage.

questions.stem: The office at Seagrape Bay Secondary School is creating a database to track daily attendance for every form class. Which item of information is ESSENTIAL?
options: The history of the school's founding
Each student's ID number and the dates they were present or absent
A teacher's remark that attendance is "fine this term", with no daily records
questions.explain: Attendance cannot be recorded without student IDs and dates, so they are essential. The teacher's remark is cosmetic: tempting because it sounds like attendance information, but it masks the missing daily records.

questions.stem: A working group planning a new bus route from Gros Islet to Castries is handed a note on the colours the island's buses were painted in 1985. For this problem, the note is BEST described as information that
options: must be obtained before the problem can be solved
improves the solution but is not required
looks useful but masks missing information
has no bearing on the problem being solved
questions.explain: The 1985 bus colours have no bearing on where the new route should run, so the note is extraneous. Option C describes cosmetic information, the most common confusion: cosmetic information looks necessary or helpful while masking missing facts, but this note does not even look relevant to the route.

questions.stem: A student in Port of Spain planning a trip to Jamaica uses a travel website that earns commission from one airline ranks that airline's flights first, describing them as "the only sensible choice". This information should be treated with caution mainly because of
questions.explain: The site gains from the reader choosing that airline and uses loaded language: bias. Completeness is tempting because other airlines may be downplayed, but the root cause is the commercial motive.

questions.stem: A Coralstone College lecturer tells her class that the marine science article they are using on coral bleaching near Tobago is refereed. Which statement about this article is CORRECT?
options: It must be more current than online news about the coral.
It must have been printed on paper.
It was reviewed by independent experts before publication.
questions.explain: Refereed means independent expert review before publication. Option A is tempting, but review reduces errors rather than guaranteeing none; the article could also be online, and peer review is slow, so news may be more current.

questions.stem: A family in Barbados uses a 2011 price list to budget for a new refrigerator. The main weakness of this information is its
questions.explain: Prices from 2011 are out of date: a currency problem. Cultural context is tempting, but nothing suggests the list came from another country.

questions.stem: Montego Bay Logistics in Kingston has two proposals for its parcel-tracking system: one team will follow Waterfall, the other Agile software development. Which characteristic BEST distinguishes the two approaches?
options: Waterfall involves the customer continuously, whereas Agile involves the customer only at the end
Waterfall welcomes changing requirements, whereas Agile freezes requirements early
Waterfall completes each stage before the next begins and delivers the system once, whereas Agile delivers working software in short iterations
Waterfall produces no documentation, whereas Agile produces detailed documentation
questions.explain: Waterfall is sequential with one final delivery; Agile delivers working software every short iteration. Option A reverses the two models’ customer involvement, a common mix-up.

questions.stem: A Tortola bakery owner wants a website but says, "I can’t describe it, but I’ll know it when I see it." Which model is MOST suitable?
options: None, as the requirements are too unclear to begin
questions.explain: A prototype gives the owner something to see and react to, clarifying vague requirements. Incremental (A) is tempting but assumes the core requirements are already known.

questions.stem: Caribbean Islands Credit Union is having its member app built in increments: balances first, then transfers, then loans. Which of the following is a DISADVANTAGE the credit union may face with this approach?
options: The loans increment may not integrate easily with the earlier balances and transfers increments
Members must wait until the end to use any part of the app
Requirements must be completely frozen before any work starts
Members cannot give feedback until the final delivery
questions.explain: Integration difficulties between increments are a recognised drawback. Options B, C and D describe Waterfall; B is tempting because it sounds like a general weakness, but members can use the balances increment early.

questions.stem: The owner of the Island Hop Tours in Montego Bay reads that Agile values "responding to change over following a plan". For her excursion-app project, this means that
options: plans are made but adapted as her requirements change
the plan is fixed at the start and followed exactly
she is not allowed to change requirements
her developers will never make plans
questions.explain: The Manifesto values responding to change more highly, but plans still exist and are revised each iteration. Option D is the common misconception that Agile has no planning.

questions.stem: Developer A builds quick kiosk screens for St. Kitts tourism board and discards them once the board agrees what it wants. Developer B keeps improving a catalogue model for the King George V Street Jewellers until it goes live. Which statement is correct?
options: A’s prototype can be used only in Waterfall projects and B’s only in Agile projects
Both are throwaway prototypes, because every prototype is discarded in the end
A built a throwaway prototype, discarded once requirements were clear; B built an evolutionary prototype refined into the final system
A built an evolutionary prototype and B built a throwaway prototype
questions.explain: The difference is what happens to the prototype: discarded (A, throwaway) versus refined into the final system (B, evolutionary). Option D is tempting because it uses the right terms, but reverses them.

questions.stem: The project manager at the Harbourview Clinic in Bridgetown pins the SDLC stages on the office wall, in the order given in the CAPE IT syllabus, so that staff can follow the project. Which list should she use?
options: Feasibility study, design, analysis, development, review, implementation
Analysis, feasibility study, design, implementation, development, review
Feasibility study, analysis, design, development, implementation, review
Analysis, design, feasibility study, development, implementation, review
questions.explain: The syllabus order is feasibility study, analysis, design, development, implementation, review. Option B is tempting because studying the clinic's current system seems like the first step, but the feasibility study must first decide whether the project is worth doing.

questions.stem: A feasibility study finds that the staff of a Curaçao insurance office are strongly opposed to a new claims system, fear for their jobs and may not adapt to it. Using the five feasibility types from the class slides, this finding relates to
questions.explain: Whether users can adapt, including their attitudes and resistance, is social/behavioural feasibility (some textbooks fold it into operational). Economic (B) is tempting because resistance may cost money, but economic feasibility asks whether benefits justify cost.

questions.stem: Bridgetown Ferry Line wants its booking system checked against what was required. Its test plans are drawn up from the design specification and handed over with the coded system and the manuals. In which syllabus SDLC stage are the test plans delivered?
questions.explain: Test plans are a deliverable of development, alongside the coded system and the user and technical manuals, and they are run in testing, which the syllabus places inside development. Implementation (B) is tempting because acceptance may finish near go-live, but implementation installs and changes over to a system that has already been tested.

questions.stem: Island Pharmacy chain keeps its old stock system running in all its branches while only the key parts of the new system, receiving deliveries and reordering, run alongside it until fully tested. Then it switches over completely. Which changeover method is this?
questions.explain: Pilot running runs key parts of the new system alongside the old until fully tested, a compromise between direct and parallel. Parallel (B) is the tempting distractor, but parallel running keeps the whole of both systems side by side until the new one is fault free.

questions.stem: A new IT contractor at the Montego Bay Water Sports shop must add a field for life-jacket size to the booking database without breaking existing reports. Which item would she MOST likely find in the technical manual rather than the user manual?
options: A data dictionary describing every field in the database
A list of frequently asked questions from cashiers
An explanation of the error message "Invalid PIN"
Instructions for printing a daily sales report
questions.explain: A data dictionary is for developers and IT staff, such as the contractor, who maintain the system. Option C is tempting because error messages sound technical, but explaining them to shop staff is a user manual task.

questions.stem: Coral Reef Resorts group is replacing its booking system. Its analyst needs answers to the same 12 rating-scale questions from 250 staff working different shifts at its hotels across Jamaica. Which fact-finding tool is MOST suitable?
questions.explain: A questionnaire reaches many people on different shifts cheaply and gives comparable quantitative answers. A structured interview (B) also asks the same questions but would take far too long for 250 people.

questions.stem: An analyst spends a morning watching data-entry clerks at the Bridge Street Insurance office in Castries. The clerks work faster and make fewer errors than the office's records show for a normal day. This problem is known as
questions.explain: The Bridge Street Insurance clerks changed their behaviour because they knew they were being watched: the Hawthorne effect. Interviewer bias (B) is tempting but concerns how an interviewer influences answers, not observed behaviour.

questions.stem: At Island Code Studio, one analyst draws a Booking class listing bookingID, pickupDate and calculateCost(). Another draws BOOKING and VEHICLE entities with their attributes and a 1:M relationship. Which statement BEST distinguishes the first model (an object model) from the second (an ER diagram)?
options: The object model shows operations (methods) as well as data.
The object model shows only the relationships between entities.
The object model shows data stores and data flows.
The object model shows tasks against time.
questions.explain: The Booking class includes the method calculateCost() alongside its attributes; the ER diagram shows data and relationships only. A describes a DFD, the most tempting distractor because both are modelling tools.

questions.stem: The project manager for a new stock system at the Barbadian Medical Supplies draws a Gantt chart. Task P (system design) runs from week 4 to week 7 and Task Q (program coding) runs from week 6 to week 9. Which statement is TRUE?
options: P lasts 4 weeks and the tasks overlap in week 7 only.
P lasts 3 weeks and the tasks do not overlap.
P lasts 4 weeks and the tasks overlap in weeks 6 and 7.
P lasts 3 weeks and the tasks overlap in weeks 6 and 7.
questions.explain: P: 7 − 4 + 1 = 4 weeks; both bars appear in weeks 6 and 7. D is tempting for candidates who forget to add 1 when calculating duration.

questions.stem: Analysts at Caribbean Code Works in Bridgetown, Barbados, need software to draw the DFDs for a new hospital records system and to keep a central data dictionary of every field. Which type of CASE tool would MOST likely provide these facilities?
questions.explain: Upper CASE supports analysis and design, which is where DFDs and the data dictionary are produced. Lower CASE (A) supports coding and testing, so it is the tempting but wrong choice.

questions.stem: A systems analyst studying the Seaside Pharmacy in Frigate Bay draws a diagram showing where prescription data comes from, which processes change it, where it is stored and who receives the results. This is a data flow diagram, which is BEST defined as
options: a diagram showing the sequence of steps and decisions in a program
a diagram of the hardware and network links in a system
a graphical representation of how data moves into, through and out of a system, showing entities, processes, stores and flows
a chart showing the schedule of tasks in a systems project
questions.explain: The analyst's diagram models the flow of prescription data, so it is a DFD. Option A is tempting but describes a flowchart, which shows sequence and decisions; a DFD shows neither.

questions.stem: In a Gane and Sarson DFD for Blue Channel Ferries in San Pedro, a rectangle with rounded corners is divided by a line and contains "2.0" and "Validate booking". This symbol represents
questions.explain: Rounded rectangle + number + verb phrase = process: validating the passenger's booking transforms data. A data store (D) is tempting because it also has an identifier, but stores are open-ended rectangles numbered D1, D2.

questions.stem: A CAPE student at Bayleaf Hill Secondary has drawn the context level DFD for King George V Street Pharmacy and now draws its level 1 DFD. Which feature will appear on her level 1 DFD that was NOT on the context level DFD?
questions.explain: Data stores such as the pharmacy's Prescriptions file first appear at level 1. Option B is tempting, but the context level does have a process: exactly one, numbered 0.

questions.stem: In a draft payroll DFD for the Blue Water Marine Services in Kralendijk, process 3.0 "Print payslip" sends a payslip to Employee, but no data flows into it. This error is called
questions.explain: The payslip appears from nothing: outputs with no inputs is a miracle. Option B is the most tempting distractor, but a black hole is the reverse: inputs with no outputs.

questions.stem: At the Palmetto Point Secondary canteen, a student sends her lunch choice from her phone to the pre-order system. Which label is CORRECT for this data flow on the DFD?
questions.explain: The student's lunch choice is data, so the flow takes a noun phrase: "order details". "Record order" (B) is tempting because it looks correct, but it is a verb phrase suitable for a process, not a flow.

questions.stem: A trainee at the Georgetown Insurance Brokers lists what makes his algorithm for calculating premiums "well designed". Which item on his list is NOT a characteristic of a well-designed algorithm in the CAPE syllabus?
options: It is written in a high-level programming language
Its steps are clearly defined and unambiguous
It has a finite number of steps
questions.explain: The trainee is wrong about C: algorithms are language-independent plans; coding his premium algorithm in a language would produce a program. Option C is tempting if students think long processes are fine, but finiteness is a required characteristic: the algorithm must end.

questions.stem: An algorithm for the Bonaire Boat Tours reads: "1. Get the number of passengers. 2. Multiply 10 by $35. 3. Display the cost." Which characteristic does it lack?
questions.explain: Step 2 uses a fixed 10 passengers instead of the number obtained, so it works for one case only. Flow of control is tempting, but the steps are in a sensible order; the fault is the fixed value.

questions.stem: In a flowchart for the Gros Islet Hardware till, one step works out what a customer owes: "total ← price * quantity". In which symbol should this step be drawn?
questions.explain: Working out the customer's total is a calculation, which is a process, drawn as a rectangle. The parallelogram is tempting because price and quantity are data, but it is used only when data is input or output, not processed.

questions.stem: Two clerks at Curaçao Tour Desk follow the same written booking algorithm but read one step differently, so they quote different prices for the same tour. Which representation of an algorithm is MOST likely to cause this problem?
questions.explain: Everyday words can carry more than one meaning, so the two clerks can each interpret a sentence their own way. Pseudocode is tempting for students who find it hard to read, but its structured statements are precise.

questions.stem: Before coding a booking system for a guest house in Holetown, the team at the software firm Bay Logic writes and agrees an algorithm. Which statement BEST describes the role of that algorithm?
options: It is a plan for the solution that the program is later developed from
It is used only after the program has been tested
It replaces the need for a program
It is the final executable form of the solution
questions.explain: Bay Logic's algorithm is the plan or blueprint that comes before the booking program. Option D is tempting but describes a program, not an algorithm.
