options: Doubt its currency and look for a more recent source
Accept it, because it has a copyright sign
Reject it, because it names an author
questions.explain: A 2018 copyright with no later update warns that the rules may have changed.

questions.topic: Characteristics of sources and criteria for selecting them
questions.stem: A page on coral bleaching links to refereed studies and is linked from a university library guide.
options: Reliable links in both directions support selecting it
Links prove the page is refereed
Links make no difference to selection
questions.explain: Links to reliable pages show knowledge of the literature; links from reliable pages show that authorities trust it.

questions.topic: Characteristics of sources and criteria for selecting them
questions.stem: Andre, a Sea-Almond Secondary School student, must select one web source on safe hurricane shutters for a class report. Which page BEST meets the criteria for selecting information from the Internet?
options: A page with a million views and animated graphics, but no author or date.
A page on a regional engineering institute's .edu site that names its author, shows "Last updated: March 2026", offers a Webmaster contact and is linked from a university library guide.
www.shutterdeals.com/sale: no author, no date, and links only to its own shop.
www.freepages-host.com/~andyfixit/shutters.html: a personal page with no contact details.

questions.topic: Characteristics of sources and criteria for selecting them
questions.stem:
Each statement is about a source on Hurricane Irma recovery. Decide whether it describes the source (a characteristic, SO 1.5) or applies a test to decide whether to select it (a criterion, SO 1.6).

Describing the source, or testing it for selection?

The report is a 90-page PDF on a government web site.
questions.explain: It states format and medium: a description.

questions.topic: Characteristics of sources and criteria for selecting them
questions.stem:
Describing the source, or testing it for selection?

The report costs nothing to download.
questions.explain: It states the cost: a description.

questions.topic: Characteristics of sources and criteria for selecting them
questions.stem:
Describing the source, or testing it for selection?

The report was written by a construction firm hoping to win rebuilding contracts, so its recommendations may favour that firm.
questions.explain: It tests the source for bias to decide whether to rely on it.

questions.topic: Characteristics of sources and criteria for selecting them
questions.stem:
Describing the source, or testing it for selection?

The report covers every district of Dutch Sint Maarten.
questions.explain: It describes the breadth of coverage.

questions.topic: Characteristics of sources and criteria for selecting them
questions.stem:
Describing the source, or testing it for selection?

The report leaves out the French side, so it is not enough for a whole-island study.
questions.explain: It applies the completeness test against the user's purpose.

questions.topic: Characteristics of sources and criteria for selecting them
questions.stem:
Describing the source, or testing it for selection?

Its damage figures do not match the official statistics, so they need checking before use.
questions.explain: It applies the accuracy test.

questions.topic: Characteristics of sources and criteria for selecting them
questions.stem:
Describing the source, or testing it for selection?

It was published in 2018.
questions.explain: It simply states currency: a description.

questions.topic: Characteristics of sources and criteria for selecting them
questions.stem:
Describing the source, or testing it for selection?

It was not reviewed by independent experts, so it should be balanced with a refereed study.
questions.explain: It applies the refereed or un-refereed criterion.

questions.topic: Characteristics of sources and criteria for selecting them
questions.stem:
You are a student intern helping the Mandeville Residents' Association in Jamaica prepare a short report on recent electricity outages in the area, to present at a public meeting. Choose your sources wisely.

Your first search finds a viral social media post saying "The power company has had 40 outages this month and is hiding it". It has thousands of shares. What do you do?
options: Treat it as an unverified claim and look for an original, accountable source for the outage figures.
Use the figure of 40 outages as the headline of the report because so many people shared it.

questions.topic: Characteristics of sources and criteria for selecting them
questions.stem: You find two more sources: the power company's outage notice page with dated entries, and a 2014 overseas magazine article on power grids in the US Midwest. Which do you select?
options: The magazine article, because it explains grids in detail.
The power company's dated notices, cross-checked with residents' own records of outage dates.

questions.topic: Characteristics of sources and criteria for selecting them
questions.stem: A board member hands you a leaflet from the PowerSafe Generators Ltd claiming outages will double next year. How do you treat it?
options: Note the company's commercial interest, treat the prediction as biased, and seek an independent or refereed source on future supply.
Include the prediction as a fact; it comes from a company that knows about power.

questions.topic: Characteristics of sources and criteria for selecting them
questions.stem: A web page about Caribbean scholarship deadlines has no author name, no date, several broken links and adverts for loan companies. Which characteristic of information on the Internet does this page MOST clearly warn the student about?
options: Internet information is refereed because it is published publicly.
Anyone can publish online without review, so authorship, currency and purpose must be checked.
Internet information is always free of cost.
Internet information is always more current than printed information.

questions.stem:
Organisations around the Caribbean process very different kinds of data. Sort each situation by the kind of data being processed.

Business data or scientific data?

The Bayside Resort in English Harbour prints payslips for 600 staff every fortnight using the same pay calculation.
questions.explain: The same processing repeated every pay run, with a large volume of output: business data.

questions.stem:
Business data or scientific data?

The electricity company in Grenada produces a bill for every customer account on the island.
questions.explain: Thousands of bills from the same calculation: business data needing large volumes of output.

questions.stem:
Business data or scientific data?

The Island Savings Bank in Roseau prints a monthly statement for each of its 20,000 account holders.
questions.explain: Repeated every month, huge output: business data.

questions.stem:
Business data or scientific data?

The Frederick Street Jewellers produces the same daily sales report for each of its three branches.
questions.explain: A routine report run again and again: business data.

questions.stem:
Business data or scientific data?

Forecasters run computer models on wind and pressure readings to predict where a tropical storm will be in 48 hours.
questions.explain: Millions of calculations, and the output is needed fast: scientific data.

questions.stem:
Business data or scientific data?

A seismograph network in the Eastern Caribbean records ground movement every second and calculates where an earthquake started.
questions.explain: Numerous computations with results needed at once: scientific data.

questions.stem:
Business data or scientific data?

Researchers at the Saba Reef Project calculate water-temperature trends from thousands of sensor readings to warn of coral bleaching.
questions.explain: Heavy computation on measurements, with a fast warning needed: scientific data.

questions.stem:
Business data or scientific data?

Students in a Coralstone College physics practical log a temperature every second and calculate the cooling rate as the experiment runs.
questions.explain: Many calculations on readings, with results while the experiment is running: scientific data.

questions.stem:
The Gouyave Bakery still runs its orders and accounts by hand. Sort each statement about its manual system.

Is this a strength or a problem of manual processing?

A new assistant learns the order book in one morning because the method is so simple.
questions.explain: Manual methods are simple and require little training.

questions.stem:
Is this a strength or a problem of manual processing?

The owner designs her own order sheets and decides how to handle each unusual cake order.
questions.explain: Greater creativity: people shape how the data is handled.

questions.stem:
Is this a strength or a problem of manual processing?

When the bakery opened, a computer system was unaffordable, but a notebook and pen cost almost nothing.
questions.explain: Manual methods suit places where technology is unavailable or unaffordable.

questions.stem:
Is this a strength or a problem of manual processing?

Staff feel involved in every order and are more inclined to work.
questions.explain: People are often more inclined to work when they handle each step themselves.

questions.stem:
Is this a strength or a problem of manual processing?

Getting the week's orders ready to be totalled takes the whole of Monday morning.
questions.explain: Slow to get data ready for processing.

questions.stem:
Is this a strength or a problem of manual processing?

The order book was soaked when the roof leaked during a storm.
questions.explain: Paper holding the data needs protection.

questions.stem:
Is this a strength or a problem of manual processing?

Each regular customer's name and address is rewritten on every new order sheet.
questions.explain: Reusing data is repetitive in a manual system.

questions.stem:
Is this a strength or a problem of manual processing?

To find every order for coconut tarts last month, the owner must read every page.
questions.explain: Querying information is difficult by hand.

questions.stem:
Is this a strength or a problem of manual processing?

Totals added by hand at the end of a long day often contain mistakes.
questions.explain: Manual processing is slow and errors may occur in the output.

questions.stem: At Bartica Clinic, a patient's name, address and date of birth are typed once at registration. The same stored details then appear automatically on every prescription, appointment letter and invoice for years. Which benefit of automated processing does this BEST show?

Caribbean organisations process data in different ways. For each one, decide whether the system described is fully manual, fully automated, or a mix of both.

At Gouyave Bakery, the owner writes each order in a notebook, adds the day's totals with a pocket calculator and pins the order list to the wall.
questions.explain: Manual. A handheld calculator is a tool used by a person; every stage is carried out by hand.

questions.stem: At the Bayside Car Rental desk at Grantley Adams International Airport, customers book online, the system calculates the charge, emails a confirmation and saves every booking to a cloud database.
questions.explain: Automated. Input, processing, output and storage are all done by software, with staff supervising.

questions.stem: A Mathematics teacher at Coralstone College marks tests by hand, then types the scores into a spreadsheet that calculates the class average.
questions.explain: Mixed. Marking and entry are manual; the calculating is automated.

questions.stem: The Frigate Bay Hardware store scans barcodes at the till, but once a month the manager counts the stock in the yard by hand and writes the totals in a ledger.
questions.explain: Mixed. Sales capture is automated; the stock count and ledger are manual.

questions.stem: A rain gauge in Jamaica sends a reading every minute to a computer, which plots a rainfall graph and publishes it on a website without anyone touching it.
questions.explain: Automated. A sensor captures the data and software processes and disseminates it.

questions.stem: At Seaside Pharmacy, a clerk takes the week's raw till entries such as "Panadol 24s, 1, US$6.50", groups them by product with pen and paper, and writes out a best-sellers list for the manager.
questions.explain: Manual. The clerk turns raw data into information by hand: grouping, totalling and writing the report.

questions.stem:
Manual and automated processing each have strengths. Read each Caribbean situation and decide which approach has the advantage.

Which approach suits this situation better?

After a storm knocks out power and the network, a marina in Rodney Bay must still record which boats leave the lagoon.
questions.explain: Manual processing works without electricity or a network.

questions.stem:
Which approach suits this situation better?

The Island Phone Company must produce 40,000 accurate monthly bills by tomorrow morning.
questions.explain: Automated processing is very fast with large volumes.

questions.stem:
Which approach suits this situation better?

A small roadside fruit stand in Lelydorp, Suriname, makes about ten sales a day and wants the lowest possible start-up cost.
questions.explain: Manual has a low start-up cost: a notebook and a cash box.

questions.stem:
Which approach suits this situation better?

A savings bank in St. George’s must calculate interest on 15,000 accounts without a single arithmetic slip.
questions.explain: Software calculates consistently, provided the input and program are correct.

questions.stem:
Which approach suits this situation better?

A church secretary receives a donation form with an unusual handwritten note asking to split the gift between two funds.
questions.explain: Human judgement handles odd cases that a program was never set up for.

questions.stem:
Which approach suits this situation better?

The Fort Street Boutique wants staff in all three branches to check the same stock record at the same time.
questions.explain: Automated systems let many users in many places share one record at once.

questions.stem:
Which approach suits this situation better?

Once its system is set up, the Belmopan Clinic wants the lowest possible cost each time an appointment is recorded.
questions.explain: Automated processing has a low running cost per transaction once set up.

questions.stem: At Frangipani Hill Academy, a form teacher marks the class register on paper each morning. The office then types the absences into a spreadsheet, which counts each student's absences for the term. Which statement BEST describes this system?
options: It is a fully automated system because a spreadsheet is used.
It is a mixed system: input is manual and the calculating is automated.
It is not information processing because no new data is created.
It is a fully manual system because the register starts on paper.

questions.stem:
Clerks at the Gros Islet Ferry Company key passenger data from paper booking forms. Sort each mistake into the type of input error it shows.

Which type of input error is this?

A passenger wrote her fare as US$35 in untidy handwriting; the clerk read it as US$55 and keyed that.
questions.explain: Copying the wrong value from the source is a transcription error.

questions.stem:
Which type of input error is this?

A clerk copying from a faint carbon copy read the surname "Hodge" as "Hedge".
questions.explain: A wrongly copied character is a transcription error.

questions.stem:
Which type of input error is this?

A passenger's year of birth, 1954, was typed as 1945.
questions.explain: Two digits swapped places: a transposition error.

questions.stem:
Which type of input error is this?

Ticket number 4217 was keyed as 4271.
questions.explain: The 1 and the 7 were swapped: transposition.

questions.stem:
Which type of input error is this?

The clerk left the phone number field blank for a passenger travelling to Martinique.
questions.explain: A missing field is an omission.

questions.stem:
Which type of input error is this?

A whole booking form slipped behind the desk and was never entered.
questions.explain: A missing record is also an omission.

questions.stem:
Which type of input error is this?

The same family's booking was keyed in twice, so the boat showed four extra passengers.
questions.explain: Entering the same record twice is duplication.

questions.stem:
Which type of input error is this?

A passenger on a slow connection tapped Send twice and the online booking form was submitted two times.
questions.explain: Two copies of one record: duplication.

questions.stem:
Sort each input method used by organisations in Belize.

Is this input manual or automated?

A nurse at the San Pedro Clinic writes a patient's temperature on a paper chart.
questions.explain: A person reads and writes the value: manual.

questions.stem:
Is this input manual or automated?

A digital thermometer sends the temperature straight to the patient's electronic record.
questions.explain: A device captures the value directly: automated.

questions.stem:
Is this input manual or automated?

A supermarket cashier in Belmopan scans each item's barcode.
questions.explain: The scanner reads the code; the cashier only holds the item.

questions.stem:
Is this input manual or automated?

A market vendor ticks a tally sheet each time she sells a coconut.
questions.explain: Tally marks by hand are manual data capture.

questions.stem:
Is this input manual or automated?

An OMR machine reads the shaded bubbles on 400 multiple-choice answer sheets.
questions.explain: Optical mark recognition is automated capture.

questions.stem:
Is this input manual or automated?

A librarian copies a borrower's name and the book title into a loans book.
questions.explain: Handwritten records are manual.

questions.stem:
Is this input manual or automated?

A weather station sensor records wind speed every minute during a storm.
questions.explain: Sensors capture data automatically without a person.

questions.stem:
Is this input manual or automated?

A student fills in a paper application form for Flamboyant Heights College.
questions.explain: A paper source document completed by hand is manual collection.

questions.stem: The Port of Spain Taxi Association receives daily trip sheets from 30 drivers. A clerk places all the sheets for the week into a single folder, arranged by driver number, so that they can be checked together. Which processing operation is the clerk MAINLY carrying out?

Both belong to the output stage, but they are different. Decide whether each activity is about the form of the information (presenting) or about getting it to people (dissemination).

Form of the information, or distribution?

The Aruba Youth Football League turns its results table into a colour bar chart.
questions.explain: Choosing a chart is about form: presenting.

questions.stem:
Form of the information, or distribution?

The league table is pinned up in the clubhouse and shared in the parents' WhatsApp group.
questions.explain: Pinning up and sharing gets it to people: dissemination.

questions.stem:
Form of the information, or distribution?

Departure screens at Queen Beatrix International Airport show flight times in large text, with delayed flights highlighted in red.
questions.explain: Text size and colour are about form: presenting.

questions.stem:
Form of the information, or distribution?

An SMS storm alert is sent to every registered phone on the island.
questions.explain: Sending to many receivers is dissemination.

questions.stem:
Form of the information, or distribution?

A teacher at Sea-Almond Secondary School redraws a table of marks as a line graph so parents can see progress over the year.
questions.explain: Changing table to graph is presenting.

questions.stem:
Form of the information, or distribution?

The Harbour View Supermarket emails its weekly specials to 3,000 customers.
questions.explain: Emailing to an audience is automated dissemination.

questions.stem:
Form of the information, or distribution?

A radio announcer reads the hurricane bulletin aloud on the morning show.
questions.explain: Broadcasting the bulletin to listeners is dissemination.

questions.stem:
Form of the information, or distribution?

A report writer uses a table instead of paragraphs so the manager can compare branches at a glance.
questions.explain: Choosing a table is presenting.

questions.stem:
Each activity comes from the Charlestown Community Centre's youth sports league. Choose the stage of the information processing cycle it belongs to.

Coaches fill in a match sheet with each team's goals.
questions.explain: Recording data at source is input (data collection and capture).

questions.stem: The organiser works out each team's points: 3 for a win, 1 for a draw.
questions.explain: Calculating is a processing operation.

questions.stem: The league table is ranked from most points to fewest.
questions.explain: Ranking is sorting: processing.

questions.stem: The league table is posted on the centre's notice board and WhatsApp group.
questions.explain: Posting and sharing is dissemination: output.

questions.stem: Match sheets are kept in a box file for the end-of-season awards.
questions.explain: Keeping records for later use is storage.

questions.stem: Coaches complain that goal-scorers' names were missing, so a new column is added to the match sheet.
questions.explain: An evaluation that changes what is collected at input is feedback.

questions.stem:
The Pond Island Medical Centre handles patient records. Sort each activity.

Which activity is this?

A clerk files a new patient card in the drawer for surnames beginning with R.
questions.explain: Placing a record in its home is storing.

questions.stem:
Which activity is this?

The system saves each consultation note to the server the moment the doctor clicks Save.
questions.explain: Saving to a server is automated storing.

questions.stem:
Which activity is this?

A nurse searches the database for a patient by date of birth.
questions.explain: Finding and bringing back a record is retrieving.

questions.stem:
Which activity is this?

A receptionist pulls a patient's folder from the cabinet before an appointment.
questions.explain: Taking a stored record out for use is manual retrieval.

questions.stem:
Which activity is this?

An X-ray image is emailed securely to a specialist in Curaçao.
questions.explain: Sending to another location is transmitting.

questions.stem:
Which activity is this?

A courier carries a sealed folder of test results to the hospital.
questions.explain: Physically moving the record is manual transmission.

questions.stem:
Which activity is this?

A full copy of the database is made every night to a cloud backup.
questions.explain: A backup is a stored copy kept for recovery, so this is storing (it also involves sending the copy over a network).

questions.stem:
All of these information systems can be found in Dominica. Sort each one.

Is this a manual or an automated information system?

The Portsmouth Hardware keeps staff attendance in a sign-in notebook at the door.
questions.explain: Attendance recorded in a notebook is a manual information system.

questions.stem:
Is this a manual or an automated information system?

The clerk at the Roseau Freight Company calculates the wages in a ledger book every Friday.
questions.explain: Payroll in a physical ledger is manual.

questions.stem:
Is this a manual or an automated information system?

A church secretary types letters to members on a typewriter.
questions.explain: Letters by hand or typewriter, not a word processor: manual.

questions.stem:
Is this a manual or an automated information system?

At month end, the owner of the Roseau Bakery matches the receipt book against supplier invoices by hand.
questions.explain: Handwritten reconciliation of sales and purchases is manual.

questions.stem:
Is this a manual or an automated information system?

A snackette in Portsmouth rings up sales on a basic cash register and writes the bills by hand.
questions.explain: Basic cash register and handwritten bills: manual.

questions.stem:
Is this a manual or an automated information system?

A customer withdraws cash from an ATM in Roseau and her balance updates at once.
questions.explain: ATM transactions are an automated information system.

questions.stem:
Is this a manual or an automated information system?

A travel agent in Grand Anse books seats on a flight from MBIA in an airline reservation system.
questions.explain: Airline reservation systems are automated and shared worldwide.

questions.stem:
Is this a manual or an automated information system?

The Island Bottling Plant's system tracks bottles and caps and raises re-orders when stock runs low.
questions.explain: Manufacturing inventory control: automated.

questions.stem:
Is this a manual or an automated information system?

A supermarket's tills scan barcodes and update the stock file with every sale.
questions.explain: A point-of-sale system is automated.

questions.stem:
Is this a manual or an automated information system?

The Bayside Resort pays 600 staff from a payroll database management system.
questions.explain: A payroll DBMS is automated.

questions.stem:
Each situation comes from the Caribbean. Choose the advantage of automated information systems it shows, or spot the user frustration.

A grandmother in Willemstad video-calls her grandson studying in Utrecht every Sunday at no extra cost.
questions.explain: Communication: video calls are quicker, cheaper and more efficient.

questions.stem: The Belizean Crafts Co-op website takes orders at 3 a.m. while its Albert Street shop is closed.
questions.explain: Availability: the business is open 24×7, anytime and anywhere.

questions.stem: A Westpunt guesthouse lets guests from Colombia, France and the Netherlands book in their own language.
questions.explain: Globalisation and cultural gap: linguistic and geographical boundaries are reduced.

questions.stem: A Coralstone College graduate is hired as a web designer to build online booking pages for local hotels.
questions.explain: New types of jobs: web designers, programmers and systems analysts.

questions.stem: The managers of the Harbour View Supermarket use a daily sales dashboard and order only what sells, cutting waste.
questions.explain: Cost effectiveness and productivity: better information for decision-makers.

questions.stem: Staff at the San Fernando Ferry Company say the new booking system freezes at peak times since a second branch joined, and nobody trained them to use it.
questions.explain: User frustration: lack of training and poor performance as the system spreads.

questions.stem: The Kittitian Crafts Co-op on Fort Street closes at 6 p.m., but since it automated its sales with an online shop, orders arrive at all hours, including 3 a.m. on Sundays, and are confirmed without staff. Which advantage of automated information systems does this BEST illustrate?

After a major hurricane, the Roseau Neighbours Relief Group in Dominica is handing out food and water packs from a church hall in Goodwill. You are in charge of the information system. Make the best decisions.

Day 1. There is no electricity and the mobile network is down. Hundreds of families are queuing. How do you record who has received a pack?
options: Use a numbered paper register: name, address, household size, signature, and tick when the pack is received.
Wait until a laptop and power are available so everything is recorded properly.

questions.stem: Day 4. A generator is running and a donated laptop arrives. 1,200 families are on paper sheets. Donors want a daily count of packs by district, and volunteers keep finding people who were served twice. What now?
options: Keep counting the paper sheets by hand every evening.
Enter the paper sheets into a spreadsheet, one row per family, and use sort and count functions to report by district and spot duplicates.

questions.stem: Day 5. The spreadsheet is working. A volunteer suggests throwing the paper sheets away now that the data is on the laptop. What do you decide?
options: Keep the signed paper sheets filed, and back up the spreadsheet daily to a USB drive kept somewhere else.
Throw them away; one laptop is enough.

questions.stem: A manual filing system at the Spanish Town Clinic stores patient folders in alphabetical order of surname. Which request would take LONGEST to satisfy using this system?
options: Return a folder to its correct place after use.
Find the folder for a patient named Arrindell.
List all patients who were treated for dengue fever last month.
Find the folder for a patient named Richardson.

questions.stem: At the Harbour View Supermarket in Kingston, the manager reads the weekly stock report, sees that the bottled-water figure is often wrong, and has staff re-count the shelves and correct the stock records before the next report is run. Which stage of the cycle does this BEST illustrate?
options: Output, because the manager is reading a printed report.
A compulsory checking stage that every system must carry out before processing begins.
Feedback: the output is evaluated and corrections are looped back to the input stage.
Storage, because the corrected stock records are saved again.

questions.stem:
The Seaside Pharmacy in Portsmouth is setting up a new customer system. Sort each item of data into the type it should be represented as.

Which data type is this?

The customer's surname, for example Hodge.
questions.explain: A name is a sequence of characters with no arithmetic: a string.

questions.stem:
Which data type is this?

A Y or N showing whether the customer has health insurance.
questions.explain: A single symbol is character data.

questions.stem:
Which data type is this?

The price of a prescription: 24.95
questions.explain: A price is a quantity that will be totalled, so it is numeric.

questions.stem:
Which data type is this?

The customer's phone number: +1 767 555 0188
questions.explain: It contains digits, but you never calculate with it and it contains + and spaces, so it is a string.

questions.stem:
Which data type is this?

A voice message from a doctor confirming a dose.
questions.explain: Data in the form of sound is aural.

questions.stem:
Which data type is this?

A photo of a handwritten prescription.
questions.explain: An image is visual data.

questions.stem:
Which data type is this?

The number of tablets in stock: 340
questions.explain: A count that will go up and down with sales is numeric.

questions.stem:
Which data type is this?

A single size code: S, M or L.
questions.explain: One letter is character data.

questions.stem: A technician at the Mahaut Weather Station replaces an old mercury thermometer with an electronic sensor that sends readings to a computer as a stream of 1s and 0s. Which statement BEST describes the change?
options: A digital representation has been replaced by an analogue one, because the computer shows more detail.
Aural data has been replaced by visual data.
Nothing has changed: both represent temperature, so both are analogue.
An analogue representation, which can show any value in a range, has been replaced by a digital representation made of discrete values.

questions.stem:
You are advising several Dominica organisations on how to represent the information they need to share. For each situation, choose the best answer.

A gate agent at Douglas–Charles Airport must tell passengers spread across a busy lounge, many looking at their phones, that boarding has started. The best representation is...
options: a table of flight numbers on a notice board
a pie chart of passengers per gate
sound: a spoken announcement over the speakers
questions.explain: Sound reaches everyone in the area at once, whatever they are looking at.

questions.stem: The Mahaut Shutters Ltd wants to show customers, step by step, how to fit hurricane shutters correctly. The best representation is...
options: a bar chart of shutter sales
questions.explain: Video is strongest for demonstrating a process and showing movement.

questions.stem: A visually impaired student at Flamboyant Heights College needs to follow the course web page. Which representation helps most?
options: A larger table of course dates
A screen-reader voice reading the page aloud
A silent video of the lecturer
questions.explain: Sound is the right choice when the receiver cannot see or read the screen.

questions.stem: The Portsmouth Youth Club e-mails a 20-minute video of its fundraiser to members who have slow mobile data. What is the main drawback?
options: The file is very large and needs good bandwidth
Video can only show still images
questions.explain: Large file size and the need for bandwidth are the key limitations of video.

questions.stem: At the Roseau cruise pier, a spoken change of tender time is missed by a passenger standing near a noisy generator. Which weakness of sound does this show?
options: It can only be understood by experts
It is temporary and can be drowned out by noise
questions.explain: Once spoken it is gone, and background noise can drown it out.

questions.stem: Police use CCTV footage from a King George V Street jewellery store to show how a theft took place. The information is represented as...
questions.explain: Moving images recorded over time are video, which shows movement and sequence of events.

questions.stem:
Students in a Bayleaf Hill Secondary cross-subject project are labelling the notations they use. Answer each question.

The symbol ♭ on a music sheet tells the player to...
options: raise the note by a semitone
lower the note by a semitone
questions.explain: The flat lowers a note by a semitone; the sharp ♯ raises it; f means loud.

questions.stem: NaCl is an example of...
questions.explain: A chemical formula is scientific notation: sodium and chlorine.

questions.stem: In 4/4 time, which note lasts two beats?
questions.explain: A minim (half note) lasts 2 beats. A crotchet is 1 beat; a quaver is half a beat.

questions.stem: A = πr² represents information using...
questions.explain: Symbols such as π, = and the squared sign are mathematical notation.

questions.stem: Writing 3.0 × 10⁸ instead of 300 000 000 is mainly done to...
options: make the number harder to read
represent a very large number concisely
questions.explain: Standard form is a scientific notation for very large or very small numbers.

questions.stem: The five horizontal lines that music is written on are called the...
questions.explain: The stave (staff). The clef is a symbol placed on it.

questions.stem:
Members of the Canefield Signal Club are training to send and receive Morse Code by lamp and radio. Use the Morse table on the previous screen to answer each question.

A yacht anchored in Canefield flashes: .... . .-.. .--. What word is it sending?
The club wants to flash its initials, GB. Which is the correct Morse?
questions.explain: G = --. and B = -... ; .-- is W and ...- is V.

questions.stem: A trainee sends a dot lasting 1 unit. How long should a dash last?
questions.explain: A dash lasts 3 units: three times as long as a dot.

questions.stem: Between the words of a message such as STORM COMING, the sender should leave a gap of...
questions.explain: 1 unit inside a letter, 3 between letters, 7 between words.

questions.stem: A new member asks why E is just a single dot. The best explanation is that...
options: E is the first vowel in the alphabet
E was the first letter Samuel Morse coded
E is very common, so a short code makes messages faster
questions.explain: Common letters were given the shortest codes so messages could be sent faster.

questions.stem: During a power cut a fishing boat sends SOS by flashing a torch, then by tapping on a metal rail. This shows that Morse Code...
options: only works as electrical pulses on a telegraph wire
is a form of binary place value
can be sent over many media: light, sound, taps or pulses
questions.explain: One code, many media: light, sound, electrical pulses or taps.

questions.stem: A radio operator at a sailing club in Bequia receives this Morse message during a storm: .-- .. -. -.. Using the Morse table, what word was sent?
Roseau Parking Authority stores the number of free spaces in a car park in one byte. The byte currently holds 00111100. How many spaces are free?

Sort each example by the type of signal used to represent the information.

Analogue or digital?

A singer's voice travelling through the air at a beach concert in Canefield.
questions.explain: Natural sound is a continuous pressure wave: analogue.

questions.stem:
Analogue or digital?

An MP3 file of the same concert on a phone.
questions.explain: An MP3 is stored as binary values: digital.

questions.stem:
Analogue or digital?

A mercury thermometer in a clinic.
questions.explain: The mercury can stop at any height: continuous, so analogue.

questions.stem:
Analogue or digital?

Light pulses in a fibre-optic broadband cable.
questions.explain: Light on and off represents 1s and 0s: digital.

questions.stem:
Analogue or digital?

A vinyl record of an old calypso.
questions.explain: The groove is a continuous copy of the sound wave: analogue.

questions.stem:
Analogue or digital?

A text message sent from a phone.
questions.explain: Characters are coded (for example in ASCII) and sent as binary: digital.

questions.stem:
Analogue or digital?

A clock with sweeping hands.
questions.explain: The hands move continuously through every position: analogue.

questions.stem:
Analogue or digital?

A smartwatch showing 10:47 in numbers.
questions.explain: Time is shown in discrete steps from stored binary values: digital.

questions.stem:
You are helping the Portsmouth Community Council prepare information for residents as a tropical storm approaches. Choose the best representation at each step.

The council has hourly wind-speed readings for the last two days and wants residents to see whether the wind is building. How should the data be represented?
options: A line graph of wind speed against time, with labelled axes and units.
A pie chart of the wind-speed readings.

questions.stem: Next, residents need the address, opening time and capacity of each of five shelters so they can look up the nearest one. What do you use?
options: One long paragraph describing all five shelters.
A table with one row per shelter and columns for address, opening time and capacity.

questions.stem: Finally, the council must warn fishermen already at sea and older residents who do not use smartphones. Power may also fail. What do you add?
options: A colourful infographic posted only on social media.
A sound bulletin: a spoken warning on VHF and local radio, repeated on the hour, plus sirens in the district.

questions.stem: A Bayleaf Hill Secondary student is writing a program that converts customers' names to lower case for the King George V Street Print Shop. The notes say that in ASCII the code for the upper-case letter E is 69. What code will the program store for the lower-case letter g?

You are on duty at the help desk of Montego Bay Connect, a small ISP. Customers call with questions about their connection equipment. Choose the best answer for each call.

A customer in Ocho Rios asks what happens to the digital data from her computer before it travels down the telephone line as an analogue signal.
questions.explain: Digital to a transmittable signal is modulation.

questions.stem: A signal arrives on the line at a home in Falmouth and must become digital data the laptop can use. Which process is this?
questions.explain: Turning the received signal back into digital data is demodulation.

questions.stem: A family in Lucea wants broadband over their existing telephone line and still wants to make ordinary phone calls while online.
questions.explain: A DSL modem gives broadband on a telephone line while voice and data share it.

questions.stem: The Ironshore Beach Bar has no fixed line, but there is good 4G signal on the beach. It needs Internet for its card machine.
questions.explain: A mobile modem or hotspot connects over 4G/5G where no fixed line exists.

questions.stem: An office on Broad Street already has a modem, but wants its laptops, printer and phones to share the connection, with data sent to the right device.
questions.explain: A router directs data between devices on the local network and the Internet.

questions.stem: During a power cut, a home office in Ocho Rios loses its Internet connection even though the line outside is undamaged. Why?
options: Modems only work during the day
The ISP deletes the account in a power cut
Dial-up lines are always disconnected at night
The modem needs electrical power to work
questions.explain: A disadvantage of the modem: no power, no connection, unless there is a backup supply.

questions.stem: Ms. Arrindell works from home in Blowing Point, Anguilla. Her computer produces digital data, but the line from the street carries a signal that must be converted before it can be sent and converted back when data arrives. Which device performs this conversion?

The English Harbour Tours uses many communication tools. Sort each use into the correct timing category.

Does this use need both people at the same time?

A VoIP call to a cruise-line agent in Miami to confirm tomorrow’s tour numbers
questions.explain: A call is a live, two-way conversation: real-time.

questions.stem:
Does this use need both people at the same time?

An emailed invoice to a travel agency in the Netherlands
questions.explain: Email is stored in the mailbox until read: asynchronous.

questions.stem:
Does this use need both people at the same time?

A weekly web-conference meeting with tour guides on Microsoft Teams
questions.explain: Everyone joins the meeting at the same time: real-time.

questions.stem:
Does this use need both people at the same time?

An SMS reminder sent to customers the evening before their tour
questions.explain: SMS is store-and-forward; the customer reads it when convenient.

questions.stem:
Does this use need both people at the same time?

A question posted on a travel discussion forum about wheelchair access
questions.explain: Forum posts wait for replies, sometimes for days: asynchronous.

questions.stem:
Does this use need both people at the same time?

A monthly newsletter sent through a mailing list to past customers
questions.explain: Mailing-list messages are delivered to inboxes and read later.

questions.stem:
Does this use need both people at the same time?

The IT technician logging in remotely with a telnet-style command session to restart a server
questions.explain: Commands are typed and answered immediately during the session: real-time.

questions.stem:
Does this use need both people at the same time?

A post on the company’s Instagram page showing a new snorkelling trip
questions.explain: Followers see and comment on posts later: asynchronous.

questions.stem:
People across Belize and the region use online services every day instead of visiting an office. Sort each activity into the type of online service being used.

Which type of online service is this?

A nurse in San Pedro checks her account balance and pays her credit card at midnight after a late shift
questions.explain: Managing accounts and payments with the bank online: online banking.

questions.stem:
Which type of online service is this?

A father in Roseau transfers money to his daughter studying in Jamaica without visiting a branch
questions.explain: Transferring money through the bank’s website or app: online banking.

questions.stem:
Which type of online service is this?

The Broad Street Watch House sells watches to customers in the USA through its web shop
questions.explain: Buying and selling goods online: e-commerce.

questions.stem:
Which type of online service is this?

A family orders school shoes from an overseas online store and pays by card
questions.explain: Online shopping is e-commerce.

questions.stem:
Which type of online service is this?

A resident downloads, completes and submits a government permit application form online
questions.explain: Forms, permits and payments to government online: e-government.

questions.stem:
Which type of online service is this?

A small business pays a government licence fee through an official payment portal
questions.explain: Paying a government department online is e-government.

questions.stem:
Which type of online service is this?

Two Calabash Point Secondary students edit the same report in an online word processor from different homes
questions.explain: Web-based software that saves to the cloud and allows shared editing.

questions.stem:
Which type of online service is this?

A photographer saves wedding photos to an online storage account so she can open them on any device
questions.explain: Saving files online to reach them anywhere: cloud storage.

questions.stem: After a hurricane, the Carriacou Ferry Line must tell passengers that the 7 a.m. crossing from Grand Anse is cancelled. Many passengers use basic phones and mobile data is unreliable across the islands. Which tool and justification is BEST?
options: A web conference, because passengers can ask questions live
A post on the ferry line’s social media page, because it is free
A mailing list, because it reaches all subscribers
SMS, because it reaches basic phones over the cellular network without a data plan and is delivered when the phone regains signal

questions.stem:
Groups across the Caribbean use three asynchronous group tools. Sort each situation into the tool being used. Remember: forums and message boards are pulled from a website; mailing lists are pushed to inboxes.

Which group tool is being used?

Teachers across the region post under topics such as "Paper 02 tips", with replies grouped in threads
questions.explain: Topics with threaded replies: a discussion forum.

questions.stem:
Which group tool is being used?

A farmer in Guyana searches and finds a two-year-old thread that answers his question about irrigation pumps
questions.explain: A permanent, searchable archive of threads is a forum strength.

questions.stem:
Which group tool is being used?

The IT department posts "Lab B closed Friday" on the school learning platform’s notice board, newest first
questions.explain: A simple shared list of notices: a message board.

questions.stem:
Which group tool is being used?

Residents of an apartment block in Holetown post short notices about lost keys and water shut-offs on a shared online board
questions.explain: Short notices everyone reads in one place, with little threading: a message board.

questions.stem:
Which group tool is being used?

The Brades Community Cricket Club in Montserrat emails the season’s fixtures to 400 members at once
questions.explain: One message delivered to every subscriber’s inbox: a mailing list.

questions.stem:
Which group tool is being used?

A monthly alumni newsletter arrives in every subscriber’s inbox without them visiting any website
questions.explain: Pushed to inboxes: a mailing list (an announcement list).

questions.stem:
Which group tool is being used?

On a regional teachers’ discussion list, every reply-to-all lands in all 500 members’ inboxes
questions.explain: A discussion mailing list: replies go to every subscriber by email, which can cause overload.

questions.stem:
Each person below is using FTP or telnet. Decide whether they are uploading with FTP, downloading with FTP, or using telnet for remote command-line login.

Which direction or tool?

A designer copies the new pages of the San Pedro Marina website from her laptop to the web host
questions.explain: From her computer to the server: upload.

questions.stem:
Which direction or tool?

A school in Saba sends a 3 GB folder of coursework videos to the exam board’s server
questions.explain: Sending files to a server is uploading.

questions.stem:
Which direction or tool?

A photographer in Kingston sends 2 GB of wedding photos to a print lab’s server in Miami
questions.explain: Files leave her computer for the server: upload.

questions.stem:
Which direction or tool?

A technician copies a large software update from the supplier’s server to the office PC
questions.explain: From the server to the local computer: download.

questions.stem:
Which direction or tool?

An architect retrieves a set of building drawings from a partner firm’s server in Curaçao
questions.explain: Bringing files from the server: download.

questions.stem:
Which direction or tool?

A network technician in Basseterre types commands to check a router at the branch in Frigate Bay without travelling
questions.explain: Text-based remote control of another device: telnet (SSH today, because telnet sends passwords as plain text).

questions.stem:
Which direction or tool?

An IT student opens a text session to a mail server to test whether it is responding
questions.explain: Testing a network service with a text session is a common remaining use of telnet.

questions.stem: A web designer in Holetown has finished updating the menu pages for the Harbour View Café on her laptop. She now copies the files to the web server so customers can see the new menu. Which statement BEST describes what she is doing?
options: Using telnet to transfer the files, because telnet copies files
Downloading the files using FTP, from her computer to the server
Uploading the files using FTP, from her computer to the server
Using a mailing list to publish the files to the website

questions.stem:
Organisations in Antigua and Barbuda use social media tools for many jobs, but not every job suits them. Sort each use: is social media a good choice, or should another tool be chosen?

Does this use suit social media?

A Heritage Quay boutique posts photos of new stock the morning cruise ships arrive
questions.explain: Wide reach and visual content for marketing: a good use.

questions.stem:
Does this use suit social media?

The Harbour View Café answers customers’ questions in comments and shares a live video of its new menu
questions.explain: Two-way interaction and rich media: a strength of social media.

questions.stem:
Does this use suit social media?

A community group shares verified shelter locations and safety updates after a hurricane
questions.explain: Fast, wide reach for public information, as seen after Hurricane Irma; posts must be verified to avoid rumours.

questions.stem:
Does this use suit social media?

A recent graduate connects with employers across the region on LinkedIn
questions.explain: Professional networking is a key use of social media tools.

questions.stem:
Does this use suit social media?

The Bayside Clinic posts patients’ blood test results so they can see them quickly
questions.explain: Medical results are confidential. Use a private, secure channel.

questions.stem:
Does this use suit social media?

A school publishes Form 5 students’ exam marks on its public page
questions.explain: Marks are personal data; posting them publicly breaches privacy.

questions.stem:
Does this use suit social media?

A water sports company posts photos of storm damage publicly for its insurance assessor
questions.explain: Confidential business evidence should go privately, for example by email or web conference.

questions.stem:
For each scenario choose the Internet tool that is MOST appropriate. Think about timing, audience and the type of data.

A Montserrat school must send a 3 GB folder of video coursework to the exam board’s server.
questions.explain: Large files to a server: FTP upload (or a secure equivalent).

questions.stem: A Statia nurse wants to talk face to face with a specialist in Curaçao and show an X-ray image on screen.
questions.explain: Real-time video plus screen sharing: a web-conferencing tool.

questions.stem: A Dominica farmers’ group wants questions and answers about crop disease kept and searchable for future members.
questions.explain: Threaded, archived and searchable: a discussion forum.

questions.stem: A student needs to find recent articles on submarine cable damage in the Caribbean.
questions.explain: Finding information on the web by keyword: a search engine.

questions.stem: A Trinidad and Tobago charity sends a monthly newsletter to 3,000 donors who prefer email.
questions.explain: One message pushed to many inboxes: a mailing list.

questions.stem: A family in St. John’s wants to share photos, voice notes and messages daily with relatives in Rotterdam who use iPhones while they use Android.
questions.explain: Rich media across different operating systems: a cross-platform messaging tool.

questions.stem: The Sentry Hill Guest House in Saba wants to send booking confirmations, receipts and directions to guests from many countries. Which statement is the STRONGEST justification for using email rather than a web conference?
options: Email is asynchronous and keeps a written record, so guests in different time zones can read the confirmation when convenient and keep it as proof of booking.
Email is used by most people.
Web conferencing is a real-time tool and email is not.

questions.stem:
The IT technician at the Bayside Clinic in San Pedro is listing the tools in the building. Sort each into its family.

Which family does this tool belong to?

The DSL modem connecting the clinic to its ISP
questions.explain: Physical equipment that modulates and demodulates: hardware.

questions.stem:
Which family does this tool belong to?

A spreadsheet used to track monthly medicine costs
questions.explain: A program for calculation: software.

questions.stem:
Which family does this tool belong to?

A VoIP service used to call specialists overseas
questions.explain: Its main purpose is exchanging voice between people: communication tool.

questions.stem:
Which family does this tool belong to?

A webcam fitted to the consulting-room computer
questions.explain: Physical input device: hardware.

questions.stem:
Which family does this tool belong to?

A database of patient appointments
questions.explain: A program for storing and retrieving records: software.

questions.stem:
Which family does this tool belong to?

SMS reminders sent to patients the day before appointments
questions.explain: Messages to people: communication tool.

questions.stem:
Which family does this tool belong to?

A word processor used to type referral letters
questions.explain: A program for creating documents: software.

questions.stem:
Which family does this tool belong to?

A web-conferencing tool used for staff training with a hospital in Curaçao
questions.explain: Real-time meetings between people: communication tool.

questions.stem:
You advise the Blue Lagoon Water Sports in Grand Anse. A major hurricane has just passed. Make the best tool decisions.

Power is out across the area and the fixed Internet line is down. The cellular network has weak signal. The owner needs to tell 60 booked customers that all trips this week are cancelled. What do you advise?
options: Send an SMS to every customer, because it works over the cellular network without data and is delivered when phones regain signal.
Hold a web conference with all 60 customers to explain the situation.

questions.stem: A week later the generator is running and the 4G mobile modem gives a modest connection. The owner must agree an insurance claim with an assessor in Curaçao, who needs to see photos of damaged boats and ask questions. What now?
options: Use a web-conferencing tool with audio and screen sharing of the photos, switching video off to save bandwidth, then email the full-resolution photos afterwards.
Post the photos of the damage publicly on social media and ask the assessor to look there.

questions.stem: The repair team wants a simple way to share daily progress photos, voice notes and locations among six staff who use a mix of iPhones and Android phones. What do you recommend?
options: Telnet sessions to each staff member’s phone.
A cross-platform messaging group with clear rules on work-only use.

questions.stem: The Trinidadian Cricket Association is deciding whether to use a mailing list or a discussion forum to keep its 400 members informed. Which statement CORRECTLY distinguishes the two tools for the committee?
options: A mailing list can only be used by businesses, whereas a forum can only be used by schools.
A mailing list pushes each message to subscribers’ email inboxes, whereas a discussion forum keeps threaded posts on a website that members visit.
A discussion forum delivers posts to every member’s inbox, whereas a mailing list stores messages on a website.
A mailing list is real-time, whereas a discussion forum is asynchronous.

questions.stem:
Around the Caribbean you can see plenty of information technology, but not all of it is part of a working information system. Sort each example.

Is this just information technology, or a whole information system?

A box of new barcode scanners delivered to the Bayview Supermarket in Belize City, not yet unpacked.
options: Information system (tools, data, people and procedures working for a purpose)
Information technology (a tool on its own)
questions.explain: Scanners in a box are hardware only. No data, users or procedures are involved yet, so this is IT, not an IS.

questions.stem:
Is this just information technology, or a whole information system?

Bayview's checkout: cashiers scan items, the program updates stock and the manager receives a daily sales total.
options: Information system (tools, data, people and procedures working for a purpose)
Information technology (a tool on its own)
questions.explain: Hardware, software, data, users and procedures work together to turn sales data into information for the manager: an information system.

questions.stem:
Is this just information technology, or a whole information system?

A copy of spreadsheet software installed on a laptop at Calabash Point Secondary.
options: Information system (tools, data, people and procedures working for a purpose)
Information technology (a tool on its own)
questions.explain: One piece of software on one device is a tool. Nobody is yet using it, with data, for a purpose.

questions.stem:
Is this just information technology, or a whole information system?

The Harbourview school office records fee payments in that spreadsheet, following a set routine, and the bursar receives a termly list of unpaid fees.
options: Information technology (a tool on its own)
Information system (tools, data, people and procedures working for a purpose)
questions.explain: Now the tool is used by people, following procedures, to turn payment data into information: an information system.

questions.stem:
Is this just information technology, or a whole information system?

A Wi-Fi router mounted on the wall of a King Street jewellery shop.
options: Information technology (a tool on its own)
Information system (tools, data, people and procedures working for a purpose)
questions.explain: A router is network hardware. On its own it is IT; it becomes part of an IS only when it carries data for users and a purpose.

questions.stem:
Is this just information technology, or a whole information system?

A Port of Spain bank's ATM service: customers withdraw cash, accounts update instantly, and branch managers see daily withdrawal totals.
options: Information system (tools, data, people and procedures working for a purpose)
Information technology (a tool on its own)
questions.explain: Hardware, software, data, procedures, users and a network all work together to support the bank: an information system.

questions.stem:
Is this just information technology, or a whole information system?

A receipt printer sitting in a storeroom of a shop in Gros Islet.
options: Information system (tools, data, people and procedures working for a purpose)
Information technology (a tool on its own)
questions.explain: Unused hardware is information technology, not an information system.

questions.stem:
Is this just information technology, or a whole information system?

An utility's billing set-up: meter readers enter readings, software calculates each bill, staff follow billing procedures and customers receive statements.
options: Information system (tools, data, people and procedures working for a purpose)
Information technology (a tool on its own)
questions.explain: All six components work together to turn meter readings into bills and information: an information system.

questions.stem: Kayla tells her class at Mahoe Grove High School in Belize that Bayview Supermarket's "information system" is simply the new computers it bought. Her teacher says she is wrong. Which statement BEST describes the supermarket's information system?
options: An organised combination of hardware, software, data, procedures, users and network that converts data into information to support an organisation.
The computers, printers and cables owned by an organisation.
The field of study that includes Computer Science and Software Engineering.
A computer program that stores data in tables.

questions.stem:
Information systems are at work across Trinidad and Tobago and the region. Decide whether each one mainly supports business operations or managerial decision making.

What is this system mainly for?

Tills at the Bayview Supermarket in San Fernando record every sale and update stock.
questions.explain: Recording daily transactions keeps the business running: a TPS, on the operations side.

questions.stem:
What is this system mainly for?

At the Island Spring Water plant in Couva, sensors check each bottle's fill level and the computer adjusts the filling machine.
questions.explain: Controlling a physical process automatically: a process control system, on the operations side.

questions.stem:
What is this system mainly for?

Staff of Caribe Marts group on three islands edit one shared price list and meet by video every Monday.
questions.explain: Teams communicating and sharing work: an enterprise collaboration system, on the operations side.

questions.stem:
What is this system mainly for?

A teller at a Kingston bank records a customer's deposit.
questions.explain: A routine transaction: TPS, operations.

questions.stem:
What is this system mainly for?

The Bayview store manager receives a weekly sales report by department every Monday.
questions.explain: Routine reports for a middle manager: an MIS, supporting decisions.

questions.stem:
What is this system mainly for?

The revenue manager of the Island Breeze Hotel tests what-if room rates for next season.
questions.explain: Models and what-if analysis: a DSS, supporting decisions.

questions.stem:
What is this system mainly for?

The Caribe Marts CEO checks a dashboard of group profit and drills down to one store.
questions.explain: Summaries and drill-down for an executive: an EIS, supporting decisions.

questions.stem:
What is this system mainly for?

A list of only the accounts more than 60 days overdue goes to the credit manager of a Chaguanas furniture store.
questions.explain: An exception report for a manager to act on: MIS, supporting decisions.

questions.stem:
The Frigate Bay Hardware store in Basseterre uses both a TPS and an MIS. Sort each activity or output.

Is this handled by the TPS or the MIS?

Scanning a customer's bag of cement and printing the receipt.
questions.explain: Recording a single sale and producing a receipt is a routine transaction: TPS.

questions.stem:
Is this handled by the TPS or the MIS?

A weekly report of total sales per department for the store manager.
questions.explain: Totals produced on a schedule for a middle manager are MIS output.

questions.stem:
Is this handled by the TPS or the MIS?

Recording a delivery of 200 sheets of plywood into stock.
questions.explain: A delivery is a business event that updates records: a transaction.

questions.stem:
Is this handled by the TPS or the MIS?

A list of only the items whose stock is below the reorder level.
questions.explain: This is an exception report, a classic MIS output for middle managers.

questions.stem:
Is this handled by the TPS or the MIS?

A clerk entering a customer's credit payment against their account.
questions.explain: Payments are transactions recorded at the operational level.

questions.stem:
Is this handled by the TPS or the MIS?

A monthly comparison of this year's paint sales with last year's.
questions.explain: Summarising and comparing over time to control the business is MIS work.

questions.stem:
Is this handled by the TPS or the MIS?

Updating stock levels each time an item is sold.
questions.explain: Updating records after each sale is processing of transactions.

questions.stem:
Is this handled by the TPS or the MIS?

A report showing overtime hours by department for the month.
questions.explain: A summarised report for managers to control staffing costs: MIS.

questions.stem:
Is this handled by the TPS or the MIS?

Raising a purchase order to a supplier in Trinidad for 50 bags of cement.
questions.explain: A purchase order is one of the daily transactions a TPS records.

questions.stem:
Is this handled by the TPS or the MIS?

Running the payroll that calculates each worker's pay and prints payslips.
questions.explain: Payroll is a routine, high-volume, efficiency-oriented transaction process: TPS.

questions.stem:
Staff at offices and firms across Barbados and the region use computers all day. Decide whether each person is using an Office Automation System or a Knowledge Work System.

Which knowledge-level system is this person using?

The secretary at Calabash Point Secondary drafts letters to parents about the sports day and mail-merges the addresses.
questions.explain: A data worker producing and sending documents: OAS.

questions.stem:
Which knowledge-level system is this person using?

An architect at a firm in Freeport, Grand Bahama, uses CAD to design a hurricane-resistant roof for a new house.
questions.explain: A knowledge worker creating a new design with specialised software: KWS.

questions.stem:
Which knowledge-level system is this person using?

An administrative assistant at the Island Breeze Hotel books the conference room on a shared calendar and emails the agenda.
questions.explain: Scheduling and communication for an office worker: OAS.

questions.stem:
Which knowledge-level system is this person using?

An engineer simulates wind loads on a proposed jetty for the Coral Tours company before building starts.
questions.explain: Modelling and simulation by a professional engineer: KWS.

questions.stem:
Which knowledge-level system is this person using?

A clerk at the Grand Anse Hardware store scans supplier invoices into a document management system so they can be found later.
questions.explain: Document imaging and management for clerical staff: OAS.

questions.stem:
Which knowledge-level system is this person using?

A scientist at a marine research station on Saba models how rising sea temperatures affect coral reefs.
questions.explain: Scientific analysis and modelling that creates new knowledge: KWS.

questions.stem:
Which knowledge-level system is this person using?

The office manager of a company sets up a video conference between its Grenada and Carriacou offices.
questions.explain: Video conferencing is an office communication tool: OAS.

questions.stem:
Which knowledge-level system is this person using?

A designer at a Georgetown agency uses a high-end graphics workstation to create a 3D animation for a tourism advert.
questions.explain: A professional creating new graphics on a specialised workstation: KWS.

questions.stem:
You are shadowing managers at Caribe Marts group, which runs supermarkets in Jamaica, the Cayman Islands and St. Kitts. For each situation, decide which system is being used.

A logistics analyst changes the expected fuel price in a model to see how delivery costs to the Cayman Islands store would change.
questions.explain: Changing an input to see the effect is what-if analysis with a model: DSS.

questions.stem: The CEO opens one screen of colour charts showing group profit for all three islands beside regional visitor-arrival figures.
questions.explain: Highly summarised, graphical information with external data for a senior executive: EIS.

questions.stem: The CEO sees that Guadeloupe's profit has fallen, taps the figure and moves down to one store, then to its fresh-produce department.
questions.explain: Moving from a summary to the detail behind it is drill-down, a key EIS feature.

questions.stem: The Basseterre store manager receives the same fixed-format weekly sales summary every Monday morning.
questions.explain: Routine, scheduled, structured reports for a middle manager come from an MIS, not a DSS or EIS.

questions.stem: The marketing manager tests three possible Sunday opening times to compare forecast sales and staff costs for each.
questions.explain: Testing options with forecasts for a semi-structured decision is DSS work.

questions.stem: The board is deciding whether to open in Curaçao within five years and wants trends in the economy, competitors and tourism alongside group results.
questions.explain: An unstructured, long-term, strategic decision using external data is supported by an EIS.

questions.stem:
Caribe Marts group is building a data warehouse for its supermarkets in Jamaica, the Cayman Islands and St. Kitts. Choose the BEST answer for each step.

Caribe Marts wants one central place holding five years of sales, loyalty and supplier data integrated from all its systems. What does it need?
questions.explain: A central repository of integrated current and historical data: a data warehouse.

questions.stem: Sales records are copied out of the tills on all three islands. Which ETL step is this?
questions.explain: Copying data out of the source systems is Extract.

questions.stem: Prices are converted to one currency and duplicate customer records are merged. Which ETL step is this?
questions.explain: Cleaning and converting into one consistent form is Transform.

questions.stem: The cleaned data is written into the warehouse every night. Which ETL step is this?
questions.explain: Writing the data into the warehouse is Load, the final step.

questions.stem: The marketing team gets its own smaller store holding only sales and loyalty data. What is this?
questions.explain: A data mart serves one subject area for one group of users.

questions.stem: The duty manager in Kingston needs an instant snapshot of today's sales so far, without waiting for tonight's load.
options: A detailed report printed last month
A data mart of last year's sales
questions.explain: An operational data store gives an instant snapshot of current operational data.

questions.stem: The Leeward Agri-Help service lets farmers in Dominica describe the colour, shape and spread of spots on their banana leaves. The system asks follow-up questions, names the most likely disease and recommends a treatment. Which type of information system is this?

Shania is shadowing staff at Caribe Marts group for a week. Answer each question about what goes into and comes out of their systems.

The barcode, quantity and price of each item a customer buys is the major input to the...
questions.explain: Individual transaction data is the input to the TPS.

questions.stem: The major output of the TPS is best described as...
questions.explain: A TPS outputs processed transactions: receipts, updated stock and account records.

questions.stem: The MIS takes as its main input...
options: summarised transaction data from the TPS
questions.explain: The output of the TPS becomes the input of the MIS.

questions.stem: The expert system used by the pharmacy counter receives symptoms from the user and also needs...
questions.explain: The inference engine applies the knowledge base to the user's facts.

questions.stem: A forecast of next quarter's sales under three price scenarios is the output of a...
questions.explain: What-if forecasts are DSS output.

questions.stem: Aggregated group figures plus external tourism statistics are the input to the...
questions.explain: An EIS combines summarised internal data with external data for executives.

questions.stem: The system found in every Caribe Marts store, the most widely used of all, built to record each sale quickly and cheaply and to feed data to the other systems, is the...
questions.explain: The TPS is the most widely used IS: efficiency oriented, operational, and the source of data for the MIS, DSS and EIS.

questions.stem:
The Seaside Pharmacy in Gros Islet prints several reports. Sort each into the correct type.

Which type of report is this?

Every prescription filled on Monday, listed one by one with time and pharmacist.
questions.explain: Every individual record, line by line: a detailed report.

questions.stem:
Which type of report is this?

Total sales by product category for October.
questions.explain: Totals for a period condense many records: summarised.

questions.stem:
Which type of report is this?

Only the medicines that will expire within 30 days.
questions.explain: Only items meeting a warning condition: exception.

questions.stem:
Which type of report is this?

The owner asks today: "How many flu vaccines did we give to over-65s since August?"
questions.explain: A one-off question answered on request: ad hoc.

questions.stem:
Which type of report is this?

Average daily takings per weekday for the quarter.
questions.explain: Averages across many records: summarised.

questions.stem:
Which type of report is this?

Only the suppliers whose deliveries arrived more than 5 days late.
questions.explain: Only cases outside the normal limit: exception.

questions.stem:
Which type of report is this?

A list of every item sold at the counter during the evening shift.
questions.explain: Each transaction listed: detailed.

questions.stem:
Which type of report is this?

A one-time comparison of sunscreen sales in cruise and non-cruise weeks, requested for a meeting.
questions.explain: Unscheduled, on request, for a specific question: ad hoc.

questions.stem: The manager of the Harbour Fuel depot in Castries has no time to read long printouts. She wants to see ONLY the storage tanks whose fuel level has dropped below 20 per cent of capacity. Which type of report should the system produce?

You are an IT consultant for the Coral Tours company, which runs boat and island tours from Gros Islet and Castries. Recommend the right system at each step.

Bookings are written in a notebook and payments are often lost. The owner wants every booking and payment recorded accurately as it happens. What do you recommend first?
options: A transaction processing system for bookings and payments.
An executive information system with a dashboard for the owner.

questions.stem: The TPS is running. The operations manager now wants a weekly view of bookings per tour and a list of only the tours that ran below half capacity. What do you add?
options: A detailed report listing every booking, so the manager can count them himself.
An MIS that produces a summarised weekly report and an exception report of under-filled tours.

questions.stem: The owner is thinking of adding a weekly tour to Martinique and wants to test prices and expected demand under different fuel costs before deciding. What fits best?
options: A decision support system with what-if models using booking history and external data such as fuel prices.
An office automation system so the secretary can type a proposal.

questions.stem:
A student describing the information system at the Bayview Supermarket in San Fernando used words from several component lists. Sort each item into the syllabus component (SO 2.2) that an examiner would mark.

Which syllabus component is this?

The tills and the back-office server
questions.explain: Physical devices: hardware.

questions.stem:
Which syllabus component is this?

The point-of-sale program on every till
questions.explain: Instructions for the machine: software.

questions.stem:
Which syllabus component is this?

The stock database on the server (the student wrote "databases")
questions.explain: A database is organised stored data. The syllabus word is data.

questions.stem:
Which syllabus component is this?

Every product code, price and quantity sold
questions.explain: Raw facts captured and stored: data.

questions.stem:
Which syllabus component is this?

The Monday steps for running the low-stock report, specific to the question "what must we reorder?"
questions.explain: Instructions for people, specific to one question: procedures.

questions.stem:
Which syllabus component is this?

Cashiers trained to use the tills (end users)
questions.explain: End users are users in the syllabus list.

questions.stem:
Which syllabus component is this?

The IT manager who sets up staff accounts (an IT professional)
questions.explain: IT professionals are also users in the syllabus list (SO 2.8).

questions.stem:
Which syllabus component is this?

The store network linking the tills to the server
questions.explain: Communication links that let data be shared: network.

questions.stem: A Paper 02 question asks Jaden, a Calabash Point Secondary student, to identify the six components of the information system at the Island Breeze Hotel. He writes: hardware, software, databases, network, procedures, IT professionals. Which change gives the syllabus answer?
options: Add "reports", because the hotel's system produces them
Nothing: any recognised list of components earns full marks

questions.stem:
Things are going wrong at businesses around the Caribbean. For each case, choose the relationship between components that explains what happened.

New tills arrive at the Bay Street Spirits shop in Nassau, but the point-of-sale program has not been installed, so no sales can be recorded. This shows that...
options: users need a network to follow procedures
hardware needs software to instruct it
data is the same as information
questions.explain: Without software the hardware has no instructions, so it cannot process a single sale.

questions.stem: At the Seaside Pharmacy the program works perfectly, but a new assistant does not know the refund steps and records a refund as a sale. This shows that...
options: software instructs the machine, but procedures instruct the people
questions.explain: Good software is not enough: users need procedures to operate it correctly.

questions.stem: After Hurricane Irma, a Road Town shop's computers and software were undamaged, but card payments could not be approved for weeks. The broken link was...
questions.explain: The network connects the shop's hardware to the bank. Without it, the whole system stopped: it is only as strong as its weakest component.

questions.stem: A cashier at the Bayview Supermarket types 100 instead of 10 for a delivery, and the stock report is now wrong. Which relationship explains this?
options: data entered by users is processed by software into information, so wrong data gives wrong information
questions.explain: Data is the bridge between people and machine: garbage in, garbage out.

questions.stem: Front-desk staff at the Island Breeze Hotel in Holetown cannot see bookings made at the group's Oistins hotel. The component that should connect them is the...
questions.explain: The network links hardware in different places so users can share data.

questions.stem: The Calabash Point Secondary office follows a written backup routine every Friday. When a hard drive fails, the student records are restored. This shows that...
options: the network stores all the data
